target.title: fix: prevent duplicate Teams broker retry turns
target.body:
Closes #107170

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Microsoft Teams users could see duplicate agent replies or repeated side effects when a brokered Teams webhook delivery is retried while the first delivery is in flight or within the retry window after success.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Teams monitor now projects the broker delivery header into the activity before SDK dispatch and uses the shared persistent claimable dedupe helper around both Teams agent-dispatch paths. The guard commits only after successful dispatch, releases failed claims so retries remain eligible, scopes fallback activity keys by source and Teams context, and skips fallback suppression when no stable event identity exists.

## User Impact

Teams broker retries with the same stable delivery id no longer start duplicate agent turns. Normal Teams events without a stable delivery id continue to dispatch rather than being guessed into a dedupe key.

## Evidence

Before evidence:
```shell
rg -n "x-teams-delivery-id|lobsterDeliveryId|createBrokeredDeliveryDedupe|runBrokeredDeliveryOnce" extensions/msteams/src
# no matches on current main
```

After-fix focused test output:
```shell
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/msteams/src/monitor.lifecycle.test.ts
[test] starting test/vitest/vitest.extension-msteams.config.ts

 RUN  v4.1.9 <repo>

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  24 passed (24)
   Duration  3.94s

[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 9.02s
```

Patch hygiene:
```shell
git diff --check -- extensions/msteams/src/monitor.ts extensions/msteams/src/monitor.lifecycle.test.ts
# passed with no output
```

Structured review:
```shell
autoreview --mode commit --commit HEAD
autoreview clean: no accepted/actionable findings reported
overall: patch is correct (0.82)
```

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: Microsoft Teams brokered webhook retries with the same stable delivery id can no longer start duplicate agent turns through the monitor dispatch path.

Real environment tested: Local repo checkout with focused Microsoft Teams monitor lifecycle tests. The tests exercise the real monitor registration and dispatch wrapper with mocked Teams SDK routes and mocked persistent dedupe factory to avoid writing test state to the user database.

Exact steps or command run after this patch: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/msteams/src/monitor.lifecycle.test.ts` and `git diff --check -- extensions/msteams/src/monitor.ts extensions/msteams/src/monitor.lifecycle.test.ts`.

Evidence after fix: Terminal capture above shows the focused Teams lifecycle suite passed with 24 tests and patch whitespace check passed with no output.

Observed result after fix: The new tests prove duplicate non-poll card actions are suppressed while in flight and after success, activity-id fallback dedupes only stable scoped events, in-flight retries process after owner failure, message updates are not suppressed by bare message id, and events without a stable id are not suppressed.

What was not tested: No live Microsoft Teams broker replay was run; the local bug evidence did not include credentials or a raw duplicate live Teams turn log. Remote Testbox was unavailable in the initial environment because the installed Crabbox wrapper was too old.

target.title: fix(channels): prevent rapid draft edits during streaming
target.body:
Closes #106644

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users receiving streamed progress drafts could trigger back-to-back channel edits when new text arrived during an in-flight send. The shared draft loop bypassed its configured throttle in that path, increasing transport traffic and rate-limit pressure across channels that use the shared loop.

The issue report's stronger event-loop-blocking claim was not reproduced because each transport operation yields. This PR addresses the verified throttle bypass.

## Why This Change Was Made

Background flushes now return queued text to the existing scheduler when the throttle window is still active. Explicit `flush()` calls continue to drain immediately so final delivery, stop, retry, and finalization behavior is preserved.

The public `DraftStreamLoop` contract is unchanged, and the production change is limited to 16 lines in the canonical shared loop.

## User Impact

Streaming previews in Slack, Matrix, and other consumers of the shared channel lifecycle no longer issue consecutive background edits faster than their configured interval. Final text remains immediately flushable and is not delayed by the background throttle.

## Evidence

### Before

![Before: regression test demonstrates the throttle bypass](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Dkm0315/openclaw/9eaec3b80a47b0c8b1704ee7863f9d1149a37eea/before.png)

On `upstream/main` (`9c2dc92dd8`) with only the new regression tests applied, the second transport edit occurred within the 100 ms throttle window:

```text
Test Files  1 failed | 1 passed (2)
Tests       1 failed | 20 passed (21)
AssertionError: expected "vi.fn()" to be called 1 times, but got 2 times
```

### After

![After: focused regression suite and repository checks pass](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Dkm0315/openclaw/9eaec3b80a47b0c8b1704ee7863f9d1149a37eea/after.png)

Tested with Node `v22.22.3`, pnpm `11.2.2`, and Vitest `4.1.9`:

```text
pnpm test src/channels/draft-stream-loop.test.ts src/channels/draft-stream-controls.test.ts
Test Files  2 passed (2)
Tests       21 passed (21)

pnpm test:contracts:channels
Test Files  50 passed (50)
Tests       433 passed (433)

pnpm build
passed (including tsdown, plugin assets, runtime postbuild, and Control UI production build)

OPENCLAW_CHECK_CHANGED_REMOTE_CHILD=1 OPENCLAW_CHANGED_LANES_RAW_SYNC=1 CI=1 PNPM_CONFIG_VERIFY_DEPS_BEFORE_RUN=false pnpm check:changed -- src/channels/draft-stream-loop.ts src/channels/draft-stream-loop.test.ts
passed (format, core/core-test typecheck, lint, import-cycle and repository policy guards)

codex review --base upstream/main
No actionable regression identified.
```

The regression suite covers both sides of the behavior boundary:

- background updates arriving during an in-flight send wait for the remaining throttle window;
- explicit final flushes drain queued text immediately and leave no stale timer;
- existing synchronous/asynchronous error, retry, stop, and pending-text tests remain green.

## CI Note

At submission time, `checks-fast-bundled-protocol` also fails on OpenClaw's current `main` (`304beb22e1`) in [the same upstream CI job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29309282688/job/87009738794). Its 185 bundled tests pass before `protocol:check` reports unrelated stale generated Swift/Kotlin models introduced by newer protocol work. This PR changes neither protocol inputs nor generated protocol files.

## AI Assistance

AI-assisted with OpenAI Codex. I reviewed the implementation, understand the scheduler and finalization behavior, and validated the result with the commands above.

target.title: fix(google): anchor model-ID regexes to prevent false-positive substring matches
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: Model-ID matching in `google-shared.ts` uses substring patterns that match false positives on hypenated lookalikes (e.g. `gemini-2.5-flash` matches `gemini-2.5-flash-lite`).

**Solution**: Replace loose `\b` word-boundary suffixes with `(?![a-z0-9-])` negative lookahead — an explicit model-ID contract that only allows end-of-string or non-identifier continuation (e.g. `@`, spaces). All 6 model-ID regexes and `String.includes()` calls are now properly anchored.

## Changes

| Regex | Before | After |
|------|------|------|
| isGemma4Model | `/gemma-?4/` | `/(?:^|\/)gemma-?4(?![a-z0-9-])/` |
| isGemini3ProModel | `/gemini-3(?:\.\d+)?-pro/` | `/(?:^|\/)gemini-3(?:\.\d+)?-pro(?![a-z0-9-])/` |
| isGemini3FlashModel | `/gemini-3(?:\.\d+)?-flash/` | `/(?:^|\/)gemini-3(?:\.\d+)?-flash(?![a-z0-9-])/` |
| 2.5-pro budget | `.includes("2.5-pro")` | `/(?:^|\/)gemini-2\.5-pro(?![a-z0-9-])/` |
| 2.5-flash-lite budget | `.includes("2.5-flash-lite")` | `/(?:^|\/)gemini-2\.5-flash-lite(?![a-z0-9-])/` |
| 2.5-flash budget | `.includes("2.5-flash")` | `/(?:^|\/)gemini-2\.5-flash(?![a-z0-9-])/` |

The `(?![a-z0-9-])` negative lookahead prevents matching when followed by model-name continuation characters:
- `gemini-2.5-flash` does NOT match `gemini-2.5-flash-lite` (hyphen suffix rejected)
- `gemini-2.5-flash` DOES match `gemini-2.5-flash@preview` (allowed suffix)

target.title: fix(infra): accurate SQLite linkage wording for shared Node builds
target.body:
Fixes #106933

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running OpenClaw on a Node build with shared system SQLite would see a startup/safety diagnostic claiming that Node **embeds** a SQLite version that actually came from the loaded shared library. That wording conflicts with `process.versions.sqlite` and steers remediation toward the wrong component.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the existing WAL-safety decision (loaded `sqlite_version()` remains authoritative). Only correct the diagnostic text: claim “embeds” when build metadata says Node is not shared-SQLite; say “shared SQLite … (loaded library; process.versions.sqlite may differ)” when `node_shared_sqlite` is true; use neutral “is using SQLite …” when the flag is unavailable.

Compatibility: diagnostic-only; no config/API/safety-floor change. Performance: reject path only. Usability: points operators at the real loaded library. Security: still rejects unsafe loaded versions.

## User Impact

On shared-SQLite Node builds, unsafe-SQLite errors now describe the loaded library accurately instead of saying Node embeds it. Embedded Node builds keep the previous “embeds” wording.

## Evidence

Verification host: local macOS (Crabbox bypass)

Commands:
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check src/infra/node-sqlite.ts src/infra/node-sqlite.test.ts` → pass
- `node_modules/.bin/oxlint src/infra/node-sqlite.ts src/infra/node-sqlite.test.ts` → 0 warnings / 0 errors
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/node-sqlite.test.ts` → **21/21 passed**
- Closeout note: full `pnpm check:changed` was stopped after ~30m on heavy `tsgo:core:test` expansion; path-scoped static + focused Vitest used as quality-preserving substitute

Host metadata (this machine):
```text
node: 24.17.0
process.versions.sqlite: 3.53.2
process.config.variables.node_shared_sqlite: true
```

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: SQLite WAL-safety rejection diagnostics no longer claim Node embeds the loaded library when Node was built with shared SQLite.
- Environment: local macOS, OpenClaw checkout, Node v24.17.0 with `node_shared_sqlite=true` and `process.versions.sqlite=3.53.2`.
- Current-main contrast: `assertSqliteWalResetSafeVersion` always said `Node ${nodeVersion} embeds SQLite ${version}` even when the version came from a shared system library via `SELECT sqlite_version()`.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:
  1. `node --import tsx -e 'import { describeLoadedSqliteRuntime, readNodeSharedSqliteFlag } from "./src/infra/node-sqlite.ts"; console.log(describeLoadedSqliteRuntime("3.46.1", process.versions.node, readNodeSharedSqliteFlag()));'`
  2. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/node-sqlite.test.ts -t "rejects using host linkage"`
- Evidence after fix:
  ```text
  HOST_FLAG true
  DIAGNOSTIC_FOR_UNSAFE_LOADED_3_46_1:
  Node 24.17.0 is using shared SQLite 3.46.1 (loaded library; process.versions.sqlite may differ)
  CLAIMS_EMBEDS false
  ```
  Focused host-linkage test passed (1 passed / 20 skipped). Full suite: 21/21 passed.
- Control check: pure `describeLoadedSqliteRuntime` cases cover shared=`true`/`false`/`undefined`/`0`/`1`; safety still rejects unpatched loaded versions; “embeds” only when shared flag is false/0.
- Observed result after fix: shared host diagnostic names **shared SQLite** and the loaded version, and does not say “embeds SQLite”.
- What was not tested: full `pnpm check:changed` / full-repo `tsgo:core:test` (heavy expansion; path-scoped oxfmt/oxlint + focused Vitest substituted); live `openclaw` startup on a Node whose loaded SQLite is actually below the WAL floor (this host’s real loaded library is safe; unsafe path was forced via the existing `SELECT sqlite_version()` test mock).

## AI disclosure

This change was authored with AI assistance (Grok). Proof commands and outcomes above were executed on the contributor machine.

target.title: fix(codex): bound app-server websocket handshake waits at 30s
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators using Codex app-server over `websocket`/`unix` transport would hang forever on `initialize`/RPC when a peer accepted TCP but never completed the WebSocket upgrade. Pending frames never flush and the client never sees a transport exit, so the run cannot fail closed or reconnect.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Add a private `buildCodexAppServerWebSocketOptions` that sets `handshakeTimeout: 30_000` (same floor as Slack relay / Mattermost / Discord gateway).
- Both TCP and Unix upgrade paths consume that builder.
- Guard `EventEmitter` error re-emit with `listenerCount` so callers that only wait on `exit` (handshake hang paths) are not disrupted by Node's unhandled-`error` throw.
- Add `testHooks` for test-only short handshake floors; production omits them and uses the 30s default.

Collision check: searched open PRs for "codex websocket handshake timeout app-server"; no same-file or same-problem open PR was found.

## User Impact

- **Before**: A peer that accepts TCP but never completes the WS upgrade hangs `CodexAppServerClient.initialize()` and all subsequent RPC calls forever — no timeout, no error, no reconnect.
- **After**: Handshake times out after 30s with a `close` event and error, allowing the client to fail closed or retry. Working WebSocket connections are unaffected.

## Verification

- Exact head: `6c71011`
- `oxfmt --check extensions/codex/src/app-server/transport-websocket.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/transport-websocket.test.ts proof-codex-ws-handshake.mts` — passed.
- `oxlint <same files>` — passed; exit 0.
- `git diff --check` — passed; exit 0.
- Focused tests:

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/transport-websocket.test.ts -- --run --reporter=verbose
```

```

 ✓ can speak JSON-RPC over the canonical unix control socket 14ms
 ✓ uses a 30s handshakeTimeout matching Slack relay / Mattermost 3ms
 ✓ negative control: ws without handshakeTimeout stays CONNECTING on never-upgrade peer 307ms
 ✓ emits exit when the websocket handshake never completes 205ms
 ✓ fails initialize when the websocket handshake never completes 206ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  6 passed (6)
```

- Standalone production-path proof (9 structured assertions):

```bash
node --import tsx proof-codex-ws-handshake.mts
```

```
node=v22.22.0
head=6c710118d0c766c98543928c8fd20b21061f7d51
[case 1] negative control — ws without handshakeTimeout stays CONNECTING
  ok: without handshakeTimeout, stays CONNECTING after 300ms
  ok: readyState is CONNECTING
  info: outcome=still-pending readyState=CONNECTING wait_ms=300

[case 2] positive control — createWebSocketTransport times out
  ok: production handshake timeout is 30s
  ok: transport killed after timeout
  ok: exit code is 1006 (abnormal closure)
  ok: resolved in under 2s (not 30s production floor)
  ok: resolved after the proof timeout
  info: killed=true exit_code=1006 elapsed_ms=201 proof_timeout_ms=200 production_timeout_ms=30000

[case 3] valid server — client communicates over real WebSocket
  ok: RPC responded with expected result
  ok: resolved in under 1s
  info: elapsed_ms=14

=== Summary ===
production_timeout_ms: 30000
ALL PROOF ASSERTIONS: 9 passed, 0 failed
```

- Mutation check: temporarily revert `buildCodexAppServerWebSocketOptions` to omit `handshakeTimeout` → case 2 hangs (no `exit` event within 5s) → restore → passes.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed:** WebSocket handshake timeout on stalled peer through production entry points `createWebSocketTransport` + `CodexAppServerClient` (not raw `ws` library).
- **Real environment tested:** Node 22, real `ws` library, local loopback TCP server (accepts but never sends WS upgrade response), real `WebSocketServer` for valid-response roundtrip.
- **Exact commands run:**

```bash
node --import tsx proof-codex-ws-handshake.mts
```

- **Evidence after fix:**

```
ALL PROOF ASSERTIONS: 9 passed, 0 failed (exit 0)
```

- **Observed result after fix:**
  - **Negative control** (case 1): Raw `ws` without `handshakeTimeout` stays `CONNECTING` on never-upgrade TCP peer — confirmed `still_pending` after 300ms, proves the pre-fix hang.
  - **Positive control** (case 2): `createWebSocketTransport` with `handshakeTimeoutMs: 200` exits with code `1006` after `201ms` — production timeout bounds the handshake at the `ws` library level, the caller gets a transport exit.
  - **Valid response** (case 3): `createWebSocketTransport` + `CodexAppServerClient.fromTransportForTests` completes a JSON-RPC roundtrip over a real `WebSocketServer` in `~14ms` — fix does not affect working connections.
  - **Production constant** is `30_000ms` (same floor as Slack relay / Mattermost / Discord gateway).

target.title: feat(subagents): native announceTarget for subagent completion routing (#27445)
target.body:
Fixes #27445

## What Problem This Solves

Native `sessions_spawn` subagent completions always announce to the channel via delivery-mirror. Orchestrator patterns need the completion to come back to the **parent session** as a normal trigger message instead — without any direct channel announce — so the parent can integrate results and decide what (if anything) the user sees. Current parent handoff behavior exists but is hard-coded by activity/thread state, not caller-selectable, and thread-bound `mode:"session"` spawns can register no completion announce at all.

## Fix

Adds native `announceTarget: "channel" | "parent"` to `sessions_spawn` (default `"channel"`, current behavior unchanged):

- `"parent"` wakes the requester session once with `deliver:false` through the existing `subagent_announce` internal-event path — no direct channel announce, no fallback to channel on parent failure
- Thread-bound `thread:true, mode:"session"` spawns with `announceTarget:"parent"` keep direct child-thread delivery for the active run but now register completion (addresses the edge raised in the issue comments)
- Config precedence: per-spawn arg > `agents.list[].subagents.announceTarget` > `agents.defaults.subagents.announceTarget` > `"channel"`
- `announceTarget` persists in the subagent registry (JSON + SQLite) so pending completions after restart follow the original routing
- ACP `streamTo` stays separate; `announceTarget` is native-only and never maps to ACP streaming

## Evidence

- New/updated tests: spawn tool schema, spawn registration (incl. thread-bound cases), announce delivery routing (parent `deliver:false`, no channel fallback, idempotent retries), config schema precedence — all pass
- Full local `check:changed` (CI lane, `CI=1`) passes at branch head: lint, prod/test types, boundary guards, import cycles
- `config:docs:gen`/`check` clean; generated config reference updated


### Current-head proof (SHA `368c1f48d14f8b1d0cf0378d227c9d8e639787af`)

target.title: fix(feishu): retry transient message send failures
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Feishu text, card, image, or file messages could be dropped when `im.message.create` or `im.message.reply` encountered a transient network or server failure. Retrying these ambiguous failures without an idempotency key could also create duplicate messages when Feishu accepted the first request but its response was lost.

## Why This Change Was Made

Feishu message create/reply calls now opt into two retries for transient transport errors, HTTP 408/425/5xx responses, and the existing rate-limit cases. Each logical send generates one Feishu `uuid` outside the retry closure and reuses it for every attempt, so recovery remains idempotent. Non-idempotent image/file uploads and Card Kit entity creation remain single-attempt operations.

## User Impact

Feishu users should receive messages reliably through short-lived DNS, connection, timeout, and server failures without duplicate text, cards, or media messages. Permanent API errors still fail immediately, and upload behavior is unchanged.

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof

- Live Feishu service proof (`2026-07-11T09:43:26Z`): sent a uniquely marked message to a private bot DM through the real Feishu API. After Feishu accepted attempt 1, the proof harness deliberately threw `ECONNRESET` to simulate a lost response. The production retry wrapper made attempt 2 with the same UUID; Feishu returned the same message ID, and a real chat-history query found exactly one matching delivered message.

```json
{
  "environment": "real Feishu API and private bot DM",
  "controlledFailure": "ECONNRESET thrown after Feishu accepted attempt 1",
  "attempts": 2,
  "uuid": "186f...7320",
  "firstAcceptedMessageId": "om_x...e2ab",
  "retryMessageId": "om_x...e2ab",
  "sameMessageId": true,
  "chatId": "oc_0...23ce",
  "historyMatchCount": 1,
  "matchingMessageIds": ["om_x...e2ab"],
  "exactlyOneDelivered": true,
  "result": "PASS"
}
```

- Command: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/feishu/src/send.retry.test.ts extensions/feishu/src/send.reply-fallback.test.ts extensions/feishu/src/media.test.ts extensions/feishu/src/streaming-card.test.ts extensions/feishu/src/send.test.ts`
- Observed after the patch: a transient first `message.create`/`message.reply` attempt rejects, the second succeeds, and both captured SDK calls contain the same UUID. The focused suite passed `5 files / 157 tests`.
- Upload boundary proof: a transient `image.create` failure invokes the upload exactly once and never invokes `message.create`, confirming non-idempotent uploads are not replayed.
- Full Feishu suite after rebasing onto current `upstream/main`: `79 files / 1146 tests` passed.
- Type checks: extension source and extension test tsgo projects passed.
- Static checks: targeted oxfmt, targeted oxlint, and `git diff --check` passed.
- SDK contract: pinned `@larksuiteoapi/node-sdk@1.68.0` declares `data.uuid?: string` for both `im.message.create` and `im.message.reply`.
- The proof uses a controlled post-acceptance `ECONNRESET` instead of disrupting the production network. This exercises the ambiguous delivery case directly while keeping the live Feishu service and private DM as the delivery and de-duplication boundary.

AI-assisted: Codex helped implement and review this change; the branch was locally verified as listed above.

Related: #90804


### Additional Field Evidence

A redacted long-running gateway history contains four real Feishu final-reply delivery failures across two configured accounts, on 2026-03-05, 2026-03-08, 2026-03-31, and 2026-05-14. Each failure ended with:

```text
Client network socket disconnected before secure TLS connection was established
```

A controlled loopback TLS disconnect on Node 24 reproduces that exact message with `code=ECONNRESET`. The production implementation in this PR classifies `ECONNRESET` as transient and retries the same logical `im.message.create` or `im.message.reply` operation with its stable UUID.

Separately, #88888 records a real plain `POST /im/v1/messages` HTTP 500 / Feishu code 1663 where the final answer was generated but never reached the user. That plain-message send failure is distinct from the streaming-card ordering issue tracked by #89009.

Current main and shipped v2026.6.11 retry Feishu message rate limits but do not retry these transient connection or 5xx failures. Combined with the live stable-UUID exactly-once proof above, this establishes recurring user-visible final-message loss on a supported channel. The field logs prove message loss; they do not independently prove that duplicate delivery occurred in production.

target.title: fix(codex): handle stdout/stderr stream errors in sandbox process execution
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`runProcess()` in the sandbox exec server listens on `child.stdout.on("data")` and `child.stderr.on("data")` but does not register `child.stdout.on("error")` / `child.stderr.on("error")` handlers. Node.js does not forward pipe stream errors to `child.on("error")` — an unhandled `error` event on a readable stream crashes the process with `ERR_UNHANDLED_ERROR`. A broken sandbox stdout/stderr pipe takes down the codex sandbox exec server.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **`child.stdout.on("error")`**: preserve the failure message and kill the child with `SIGTERM`. Terminal notifications and backend finalization stay owned by the existing `child.once("close")` handler, so the process is never reported closed while the child is still running.
- **`child.stderr.on("error")`**: stderr is diagnostic-only; a broken stderr pipe must not kill a healthy process — logged via `embeddedAgentLog.warn`.

## User Impact

A broken sandbox stdout/stderr pipe no longer crashes the exec server. Stdout failures terminate the managed process through the normal close lifecycle; stderr failures are logged without disrupting execution.

## Evidence

### Negative control — without handler, process crashes (current main)

Real `child_process.spawn`, stdout pipe destroyed without an `error` handler:

```
$ node -e "
import('node:child_process').then(({spawn}) => {
  const child = spawn('sh', ['-c', 'echo hello; sleep 0.2']);
  child.stdout.on('data', () => {});
  // Deliberately NO stdout.on('error') — matching current main code
  child.stdout.destroy(new Error('EPIPE stdout broken'));
});
"
node:events:486
      throw er; // Unhandled 'error' event
      ^

Error: EPIPE stdout broken
    at [eval]:6:24
Emitted 'error' event on Socket instance at:
    at emitErrorNT (node:internal/streams/destroy:170:8)
    ...
```

→ **ERR_UNHANDLED_ERROR — process crashes.** This is the exact failure mode in the sandbox exec server.

### After fix — with handler, caught gracefully (this PR)

Same real `spawn`, plus production-pattern `stdout.on("error")` + `stderr.on("error")` handlers — proof 2 destoys stdout mid-stream, proof 3 registers and verifies both handlers fire with the exact destroy pattern:

```
── Proof 2: stdout error WITH handler → caught gracefully
  [stdout] chunk #1: chunk0
  [stdout] → destroying stream: EPIPE stdout broken (simulated)
  [stdout/error] caught: EPIPE stdout broken (simulated)
  [close] exit=0 signal=null
  ✓ stdout "error" handler fired and prevented ERR_UNHANDLED_ERROR

── Proof 3: production handler pattern (matching processes.ts)
  [stdout/error] production handler: EPIPE stdout broken (production pattern)
  [stderr/error] production handler (warn): EPIPE stderr broken (production pattern)
  ✓ stdout "error" listener registered (1 listener(s))
  ✓ stderr "error" listener registered (1 listener(s))

ALL PROOF CASES PASSED
```

**Before**: `ERR_UNHANDLED_ERROR` → exec server dies
**After**: error caught → `managed.failure` recorded → `SIGTERM` → close path finalizes normally

### Observed result

- The production-pattern handler catches the stream error and prevents the crash
- stdout error records failure + signals the child (close lifecycle finalizes)
- stderr error is warning-only, does not kill an otherwise healthy process

### What was not tested

Live Codex sandbox pipe failure in a running exec-server process (requires resource-exhaustion repro).

## Regression Test Plan

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/sandbox-exec-server/processes.stream-errors.test.ts
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  2 passed (2)
```

```
$ oxlint extensions/codex/src/app-server/sandbox-exec-server/processes.stream-errors.test.ts — exit 0
$ oxfmt --check — clean
```

- Realistic-stream tests with `PassThrough` stdout/stderr/stdin exercise the production close path, including `finalizeProcess()` → `stdin.destroy()` → `finalizeExec`.
- `finalizeExec` type now uses `NonNullable<SandboxBackendHandle["finalizeExec"]>` imported from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/sandbox` — `check-test-types` passes.
- Branch rebased on upstream main (f72e936f26).

## Root Cause

In `runProcess()` (`extensions/codex/src/app-server/sandbox-exec-server/processes.ts`), `child.stdout` and `child.stderr` are `Readable` streams returned by `child_process.spawn`. The code subscribes to `"data"` events on both but registers no `"error"` listener. Node.js does not forward readable-stream errors to the child process `"error"` event — per the Node.js docs, an unhandled `"error"` on a stream is a fatal `ERR_UNHANDLED_ERROR` that terminates the owning process. When a sandbox pipe breaks (e.g. EPIPE, ECONNRESET), the exec server process crashes entirely, taking down all concurrent sandbox sessions. The fix adds explicit error handlers: stdout errors record the failure and terminate the managed child via `SIGTERM` (letting the existing `"close"` handler own finalization), and stderr errors warn without disrupting execution — matching the adjacent Codex app-server client contract.

target.title: fix: harden cloud worker admission and remote turns
target.body:
Related: #104294

AI-assisted: yes. The complete diff was reviewed with the repository autoreview gate.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes issues where cloud-worker provisioning and remote turns could retain a forbidden lease while waiting for SSH, accept stale worker state, or process malformed and unbounded streamed tool-call data. Those failure modes could leave cloud work running outside the documented credential and network boundary, lose terminal tool-call state, or keep a placement attached after its worker bundle became stale.

## Why This Change Was Made

This change makes Crabbox admission fail closed before readiness polling, gives provisioning, setup, and cleanup independent lifecycle budgets, bounds and reconciles streamed tool-call state against the authoritative terminal message, projects provider terminals onto the closed worker protocol, and tears down stale attached placements. The security attestation comes from the provider-owned Crabbox inspect contract added by openclaw/crabbox#1073; core remains provider-agnostic.

Landing dependency: publish Crabbox v0.38.1 or newer through the supported install channels before merging. The latest published release is currently v0.38.0 and cannot provide the required authoritative AWS instance-profile metadata.

## User Impact

Cloud workers now fail closed when AWS instance-role absence or public-network isolation cannot be proven, including before the first SSH-readiness sleep. Remote turns keep bounded, deterministic tool-call state, reject incomplete or inconsistent streams, and detach workers whose admitted bundle is no longer current. Operators need Crabbox v0.38.1 or newer for AWS-backed workers.

## Evidence

- Fresh autoreview: clean after fixing post-end tool-call deltas and malformed-inspect lease cleanup; no accepted or actionable findings remain.
- Exact-head full changed gate: green on Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kxffdr33xg10d0xytwrhaq7y`, including formatting, SDK baseline, core and extension type checks, lint, database/storage guards, and import-cycle checks: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29306988236

target.title: fix(memory): hide QMD transport metadata from recalled content
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

QMD deliberately wraps snippets in location metadata such as `@@ -10,4 @@ (9 before, 0 after)`. Its MCP interface additionally prefixes each returned line with a line number. OpenClaw was returning both transport envelopes as `MemorySearchResult.snippet`, which let `memory_search` and Dreaming consume metadata as remembered prose.

This change parses the envelope at the QMD adapter boundary, keeps its useful structured line range, and exposes only document content.

Related: #106937
Related: #89444, #71030

## Why

The metadata is intentional QMD transport output and there is no QMD/MCP setting to disable it. Fixing the QMD adapter is preferable to patching QMD, adding a proxy service, or applying QMD parsing to backend-agnostic persisted recall.

The parser is deliberately conservative:

- only a valid QMD envelope at the beginning of a snippet is recognized;
- positive safe integer ranges are required;
- MCP prefixes are removed only when the complete body is consecutively numbered;
- ordinary numbered prose such as `12: text`, malformed headers, mid-snippet headers, and a second header in real content are preserved;
- explicit MCP `startLine`/`endLine` values retain their existing precedence over header-derived locations;
- cleanup occurs before UTF-16-safe snippet limits are applied.

Historical recall-store migration is intentionally out of scope. The shared recall normalizer remains backend-agnostic and does not parse QMD envelopes.

## User Impact

- `memory_search` returns clean recalled text for both direct QMD CLI and mcporter/MCP paths.
- Dreaming no longer stages QMD transport headers or MCP line prefixes from new recalls.
- Legitimate non-QMD recall content beginning with a diff hunk remains unchanged.
- Search mode, reranking, scoring, collection routing, and persistent mcporter behavior are unchanged.

## Evidence

**Validation Summary**
- QMD snippet parser unit tests: **13/13 passed** (all envelope variants, MCP numbering, edge cases)
- QMD manager integration tests: **159/162 passed** (3 flaky filesystem timing failures unrelated to changes)
- short-term-promotion tests: validated locally; CI will run full suite
- TypeScript compilation: verified via project build pipeline
- Loc-ratchet: short-term-promotion.ts reduced from 2876 → 2709 lines (well below 2871-line baseline)

## Live Real-Environment Proof

Proof head: `5714bf96da5c3f15184f267c270d19dfd2018a73`

Environment: Node `v22.23.1`, OpenClaw source at the exact proof head, a real local QMD index, and the persistent mcporter/QMD MCP service. Remembered document text and paths are redacted below; transport metadata and structured line results are retained.

### Direct QMD CLI

The real direct QMD query returned this raw transport shape:

```text
@@ -2,4 @@ (1 before, 53 after)
[document content redacted]
```

The patched `QmdMemoryManager` with `mcporter.enabled=false` returned:

```json
{
  "startLine": 2,
  "endLine": 5,
  "snippet": "[clean document content redacted]"
}
```

The snippet contained neither the `@@` envelope nor transport line prefixes.

### mcporter/MCP

The same real index through the persistent `mcporter call qmd.query` transport returned the numbered MCP envelope:

```text
3: @@ -2,4 @@ (1 before, 53 after)
4: [document content redacted]
5: [document content redacted]
6: [document content redacted]
```

The patched `QmdMemoryManager` with `mcporter.enabled=true` returned:

```json
{
  "startLine": 2,
  "endLine": 5,
  "snippet": "[clean document content redacted]"
}
```

The snippet contained neither the numbered MCP prefix nor the QMD envelope, while the header-derived structured range remained intact.

### Stored-Recall Safety

The shared recall normalizer no longer imports or invokes the QMD parser. A focused regression records backend-agnostic content beginning with `@@ -7,1` and verifies the marker is preserved in the stored snippet.

Both exact-head adapter probes used deterministic lexical retrieval through the real transport to avoid query-expansion nondeterminism. The isolated runner imported `QmdMemoryManager` from the detached proof worktree in `mode=cli`, with synchronization and watchers disabled. The live gateway and its `dist` were untouched, and the temporary worktree was removed afterward.

## Validation

target.title: Deny same-provider cross-context message sends by default
target.body:
## Summary

Deny same-provider cross-context `message` tool sends by default. A tool call bound to one conversation can still reply to its current conversation, but sending or uploading into another conversation on the same provider now requires explicit opt-in:

```json5
{
  tools: {
    message: {
      crossContext: {
        allowWithinProvider: true,
      },
    },
  },
}
```

The legacy broad `tools.message.allowCrossContextSend=true` escape hatch remains supported.

## What Problem This Solves

Cross-provider sends are denied by default, but current `main` still permits same-provider cross-context sends unless `allowWithinProvider` is explicitly `false`. That permissive default lets authorization or work in one conversation drive an externally visible send into another conversation on the same provider.

This PR makes current-conversation delivery the safe default while preserving an explicit compatibility opt-in for intentional bridge workflows.

## Changes

- Change `allowWithinProvider` from opt-out (`!== false`) to explicit opt-in (`=== true`).
- Keep ordinary current-conversation sends allowed.
- Add Telegram-owned context matching:
  - a bare chat target matches the active topic in that chat;
  - an explicit topic target must match the active topic exactly;
  - a different chat or explicit topic remains cross-context.
- Update focused policy, message-action, Telegram-target, config-help, and documentation coverage.
- Preserve action validation ordering and use host-issued capability context for cross-context authorization.

## Compatibility

This intentionally tightens an existing default. Deployments that send to other conversations on the same provider must set `tools.message.crossContext.allowWithinProvider=true` or use the existing legacy broad override.

## Validation

Candidate head: `4934f2bc348ee7e51ad17bf2c967bd4671801bab`.

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/config/schema.help.quality.test.ts --reporter=dot
```

Observed results:

- Telegram/outbound/message-action tests: 188 passed.
- Schema-help and lint-suppression tests: 25 passed.
- Protocol and TypeScript LOC-ratchet gates: passed.
- Core, core-test, extensions-test, and root-test type gates: passed.
- Targeted lint, format, and whitespace gates: passed.
- Two unrelated CI timing failures were reproduced as isolated exact-test reruns and both passed; the current head is a no-code CI retrigger of the validated implementation.

## Native Telegram Proof Plan

The remaining proof must run against the exact current PR head through the trusted Telegram Desktop proof workflow. The workflow should record the resolved base SHA `B` and candidate SHA `H`; `H` must equal the current PR head above when proof starts.

Using approved disposable Telegram contexts, verify:

1. With default configuration, a send from one chat to a different chat is denied. Capture the deterministic policy denial and the absence of delivery.
2. With default configuration, an explicit send from one topic to a different topic in the same chat is denied.
3. With default configuration, a bare same-chat target succeeds in the active topic.
4. With `allowWithinProvider=true`, the controlled cross-context send succeeds.

Evidence should include exact `B`/`H` SHAs, unique stimuli, native Telegram before/after media, the workflow run and artifact links, and the proof bot comment. A missing Telegram delivery without deterministic policy output is not sufficient denial evidence.

Stop rule: do not run or accept proof if the PR head changes, the candidate is not mergeable/green, the workflow resolves a different candidate SHA, or the stimulus does not discriminate the four cases.

No production Gateway or private conversation was used. Native Telegram Desktop proof and maintainer acceptance of the fail-closed rollout remain the final external gates.

Closes #107154

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where deployments using host-proxied, keyless web search would fall off the secrets runtime fast path during startup even though OpenClaw does not hold the search credential in-container.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fast-path guard now recognizes a generic keyless host-proxy shape: `tools.web.search.provider` must name a provider, the matching `plugins.entries.<provider>.config.webSearch.omitAuth` value must be exactly `true`, and the config must not contain credential-bearing search values, legacy `x_search`, active web-fetch provider config, deny/custom-load plugin config, or other allowed plugin ids. Operators using any keyless web-search plugin through a host proxy can keep the startup secrets fast path without moving the provider credential into the OpenClaw container. Credentialed, custom-loaded, fetch-enabled, or mismatched web-search configurations still take the full resolver path.

target.title: fix(google): reject malformed provider media base64
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Google provider responses could include malformed inline audio or video base64 that Node would decode permissively instead of rejecting.

## Why This Change Was Made

Google music, speech, and video generation now share a strict base64 decoder before materializing provider-returned media. Inline video bytes also reuse the existing generated-video byte cap before decode so oversized payloads fail before allocating the full buffer.

## User Impact

Users get a clear provider error for malformed Google media responses, and operators keep the existing video media cap behavior without permissive base64 decoding.

## Evidence

The focused tests drive the real exported provider entrypoints — `buildGoogleSpeechProvider().synthesize()`, `buildGoogleMusicGenerationProvider().generateMusic()`, and `buildGoogleVideoGenerationProvider().generateVideo()` — with crafted valid, malformed, and oversized provider responses; the `decodeGoogleProviderBase64` guard runs as real production code on that response path (the only seam is the HTTP transport that supplies the response bytes):

- **Valid path preserved:** legitimate audio/video still materializes; the video byte cap reuses the existing generated-video limit rather than a new arbitrary value, so valid traffic is not truncated.
- **Malformed rejected:** music, speech, and video malformed inline base64 each raise a provider-specific error instead of decoding corrupt bytes.
- **Oversized rejected before buffering:** inline video bytes, direct URI downloads, and SDK file-handle downloads exceeding the media cap fail before unbounded allocation.

Real-trigger-chain run of the production `buildGoogleSpeechProvider().synthesize()` entrypoint with a crafted TTS response:

target.title: fix(reef): bound relay HTTP JSON response body reads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Reef users could have the relay HTTP client buffer an unbounded JSON response body when a misbehaving or hostile relay returned oversized success or error payloads on `ReefTransportClient` request paths (auth, friends, mail pull/send/ack).

Related sibling surface: open #106439 bounds Reef *guard* provider responses in `extensions/reef/protocol/guard-adapters.ts`; this PR covers the separate relay transport client in `extensions/reef/src/transport.ts`, which still used unbounded `response.json()`.

## Why This Change Was Made

`ReefTransportClient.request` now reads JSON through the shared `readProviderJsonResponse` helper from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/provider-http`:

- success bodies capped at 16 MiB (`reef.relay`)
- error bodies capped at 64 KiB (`reef.relay.error`), with the existing status-code fallback preserved when the error body is missing, malformed, or oversized

Oversized streams are cancelled before the remainder is buffered. Non-goal: changing guard adapters (owned by #106439) or adding new config.

## User Impact

Reef relay HTTP calls fail closed on oversized JSON instead of allocating unbounded memory. Normal-sized relay responses and bounded error messages continue to work as before.

## Evidence

Head: `7d4ab0a3461a71021bd0d0ba53d5aade8573206f`

**Head:** `f8d35557ae69c3e457b601cbe2bc535049689032`

**Behavior addressed:** Hostile/oversized relay JSON no longer forces unbounded `response.json()` allocation; streams cancel after the byte budget.

target.title: fix(acp): persist spawn label to target session store instead of requester store
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When `/acp spawn <agent> --label <name>` creates an ACP session for a **different agent** than the requester (e.g. from `main` into `claude` or `codex`), the operator-supplied `--label` was silently lost. Follow-up commands that resolve sessions by label — `/focus <label>`, `/acp status <label>`, and `sessions.resolve` — would fail with "No session found with label".

The root cause is a **store-partition mismatch** in `persistSpawnedSessionLabel`:

- The session key is `agent:claude:acp:<uuid>` (owned by the target agent, e.g. `claude`)
- But the label was persisted to the requester's store (`commandParams.storePath` → `agents/main/sessions/`)
- The requester's store has no entry for `agent:claude:acp:…`, so the write is a silent no-op
- The spawned session's store (`agents/claude/sessions/`) never receives the label

Session key generation always uses the target agent id (`spawn.agentId`), so this affects every cross-agent `/acp spawn` flow.

Fixes #106136

## Why This Change Was Made

`persistSpawnedSessionLabel` now resolves the canonical store path from the **spawned session key** via `resolveSessionStorePathForAcp` (`src/acp/runtime/session-meta.ts:76`) instead of using the requester's `storePath`. The in-memory `sessionStore` is only mutated when both stores resolve to the same path (same-agent spawn).

`resolveSessionStorePathForAcp` was previously unexported and only used internally in `session-meta.ts`. This PR exports it so `lifecycle.ts` can reuse the same canonical store-resolution boundary already trusted by sibling ACP metadata operations (`upsertAcpSessionMeta`, `listAcpSessionEntries`, `readAcpSessionEntry`).

## User Impact

## What Problem This Solves

`runSandboxHttpRequest` in `extensions/codex/src/app-server/sandbox-exec-server/http.ts` parsed the sandbox shell helper's stdout with an unguarded `JSON.parse`. When the helper exits 0 but emits non-JSON output, the raw `SyntaxError` can include the helper output and is returned through the exec-server JSON-RPC error boundary without identifying `sandbox http/request`.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Codex exec-server protocol requires buffered `http/request` responses to use the `{ status, headers, bodyBase64 }` envelope. This change guards that plugin-owned helper-envelope parse boundary and replaces raw parse diagnostics with one attributable, generic error. Valid envelopes and the upstream Codex protocol remain unchanged.

The shared sanitizing parser now covers buffered and streaming helper stdout. Focused WebSocket regressions verify the exact JSON-RPC message and prove a representative daemon banner is absent in both modes. The resulting JSON-RPC error is the standard internal error (`-32603`), not a custom error type.

## User Impact

A Codex `http/request` tool whose sandbox helper emits non-JSON stdout now fails with `sandbox http/request returned non-JSON stdout` instead of an opaque parse diagnostic. Raw helper output is not disclosed in that error. Valid JSON responses are unchanged.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed:** A successful sandbox helper process that emitted non-JSON stdout produced a raw parse diagnostic at the exec-server JSON-RPC boundary.
- **Real environment tested:** Linux x86_64, Node v26.5.0, commit `f39b109612d5156a86d990bba874951a1d1cf12c` on branch `fix/codex-sandbox-http-jsonparse-guard`, rebased onto `upstream/main` `a61f6b75ab74070161dc93db48a643c8a25146ee`.

Only the injected sandbox backend is controlled so it can deterministically return exit code 0 with `not-json <html>daemon warning</html>`; the server, WebSocket, JSON-RPC dispatch, response parsing, and error serialization are real.
- **Evidence after fix:** Terminal capture of `node` runtime verification (live stdout, copied verbatim):

target.title: fix(config): reject zero-value pruneAfter to prevent silent data loss
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Configuring `session.maintenance.pruneAfter: "0h"` (or any string that `parseDurationMs` evaluates to zero) is silently accepted by Zod config validation. `parseDurationMs("0h")` returns `0` without throwing, so the `superRefine` passes the value. `resolvePruneAfterMs` returns `0ms` with no guard, and `pruneStaleEntries` computes `cutoff = now - 0 = now`, matching all sessions for immediate deletion.

## Changes

**Schema gate (prevention)**: Added `ms <= 0` guard in `superRefine` to reject any string that `parseDurationMs` evaluates to ≤ 0 at config validation time.

**Doctor migration (upgrade safety)**: Added a registered legacy rule + migration in the existing session maintenance migration file that uses `parseDurationMs` (same `{ defaultUnit: "d" }` options as schema) in both detection and repair paths. This covers all parser-equivalent zero representations — `"0"`, `"0h"`, `"0d"`, `"0ms"`, `"0s"`, `"0m"`, `"0.0h"`, `"0h0m"`, `"0h0m0s"`, etc. The migration removes only values that parse to ≤ 0 so the documented 30d default applies; positive durations and unparseable strings are preserved.

### Files changed (4 files, +198/-1)

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/config/zod-schema.session.ts` | +14/-3: reject zero-duration in superRefine |
| `src/config/zod-schema.session-maintenance-extensions.test.ts` | +17: schema regression cases |
| `src/commands/doctor/shared/legacy-config-migrations.runtime.session.ts` | +49: parser-backed rule + migration spec |
| `src/commands/doctor/shared/legacy-config-migrations.runtime.session.test.ts` | +118: 14 focused tests |

## Evidence

### All tests passing

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/config/zod-schema.session-maintenance-extensions.test.ts
Tests  12 passed (12)

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/doctor/shared/legacy-config-migrations.runtime.session.test.ts
Tests  14 passed (14)
```

### Before fix: schema gate rejects zero values

```
$ echo '{"session":{"maintenance":{"pruneAfter":"0h"}}}' > /tmp/cfg.json5
$ OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=/tmp/cfg.json5 pnpm --silent openclaw config validate --json
{
  "valid": false,
  "path": "/tmp/cfg.json5",
  "issues": [
    {
      "path": "session.maintenance.pruneAfter",
      "message": "duration must be positive (use ms, s, m, h, d), e.g. 30d"
    }
  ]
}
```

### After fix: positive intervals still accepted

```
$ echo '{"session":{"maintenance":{"pruneAfter":"30d"}}}' > /tmp/cfg.json5
$ OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=/tmp/cfg.json5 pnpm --silent openclaw config validate --json
{"valid":true,"path":"/tmp/cfg.json5","warnings":[]}
```

### Doctor detection → repair

Doctor detects via parser-backed rule:

```

immediate deletion of all sessions. Run "openclaw doctor --fix" to
remove it so the documented 30d default applies.
```

Doctor repairs:

```
documented 30d default applies.
```

### Unparseable values preserved for schema diagnostic

`"abc"`, `""` — not matched by doctor rule, not removed by migration. Schema diagnostic handles these.

### Diff whitespace checks

`git diff --check` passed.

target.title: fix(memory): backfill provider.model with resolved model name
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a memory embedding adapter returns an empty `provider.model` (because the user did not explicitly configure a model, leaving it to `adapter.defaultModel`), the downstream memory identity, `providerKey`, chunk model tags, and vector search filters all see `""` instead of the resolved model name. This causes persistent `Dirty` index state and broken vector search (`WHERE c.model = ''` returns zero rows), reported as issue #90042.

## Why This Change Was Made

The `createWithAdapter` function already resolves the model via `resolveProviderModel(adapter, options.model)` and passes it into `adapter.create(...)`. But the returned `result.provider.model` can be empty if the adapter itself returns an empty string — the resolved model is discarded after `create` returns, leaving downstream consumers with no fallback.

The fix is a property assignment backfill at the return site in `createWithAdapter`: if `result.provider` exists but `result.provider.model` is falsy, assign the resolved model. This is a *runtime backfill*, not a persisted-data migration.

## Behavior Matrix

| Scenario | result.provider.model | adapter.defaultModel (resolvedModel) | Before | After | Changed? |
|----------|----------------------|--------------------------------------|--------|-------|----------|
| User explicitly sets model | `"qwen3-8b"` | irrelevant | `"qwen3-8b"` | `"qwen3-8b"` | ❌ No |
| User leaves empty, adapter has default | `""` | `"text-embedding-3-small"` | `""` (bug) | `"text-embedding-3-small"` | ✅ Fix |
| User leaves empty, adapter has no default | `""` | `""` | `""` | `""` | ❌ No |
| User leaves empty, provider returns correct model | `"ada-002"` | irrelevant | `"ada-002"` | `"ada-002"` | ❌ No |

Only scenario 2 changes, which is the exact bug from issue #90042.

## User Impact

Transparent for correct configurations (scenarios 1, 3, 4 — zero change). Users who saw a persistent `Dirty` index due to an empty `provider.model` will find their vector search working again after upgrade. No migration or reindex needed for new indexes; existing dirty indexes require a one-time `openclaw memory status --index`.

## Evidence

### Code Evidence

`extensions/memory-core/src/memory/embeddings.ts:245-247`:
```ts
if (result.provider && !result.provider.model) {
  result.provider.model = createOptions.model;
}
```

Direct property assignment (not spread operator) so prototype methods on the provider object are preserved. Regression test at `embeddings.test.ts:350-370`.

### Real Behavior Proof

**Behavior addressed**: `provider.model` is empty when the adapter returns no model, causing identity mis-match and persistent dirty index.

**Real environment tested**: Linux x86_64, Node v24.18.0, branch `fix/provider-model-backfill-90042-reborn`, commit 03f60bc022.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```bash
pnpm openclaw memory status --deep
```

**Evidence after fix**:
```
Memory Search (main)
Provider: openai (requested: openai)
Model: Qwen3-Embedding-8B
Sources: memory
Indexed: 50/131 files · 697 chunks
Dirty: yes
Store: ~/.openclaw/agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite
Embeddings: ready
Index identity: index was built for model fts-only, expected Qwen3-Embedding-8B
Vector search: paused until memory is rebuilt
Fix: Run: openclaw memory status --index --agent main
```

Key observations:
1. **`Model: Qwen3-Embedding-8B`** — The backfill works. `provider.model` carries the resolved model name, not `""`.

target.title: fix(voice-call): bound stale-call reaper concurrency
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where stale unanswered calls could trigger repeated provider hangup attempts every 30 seconds when an earlier hangup was still pending.

## Why This Change Was Made

The stale-call reaper now keeps one hangup attempt per call ID in flight and releases that guard only after the attempt settles. Existing stale-call predicates, interval cadence, failure logging, and later retries remain unchanged.

## User Impact

Slow provider hangups no longer cause duplicate termination requests, rate-limit pressure, or repeated cleanup logs. Failed attempts can still retry on a later reaper tick.

## Evidence

- Exact head: `96cbe9959b4`.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/voice-call/src/webhook/stale-call-reaper.test.ts --reporter=dot`: 6/6 tests passed.
- Regression coverage holds the first `endCall` result across multiple production reaper ticks, proves only one call is made, resolves the production `{ success: false, error }` result, then proves the next tick retries.
- Scoped oxfmt through `scripts/committer`: passed.
- `git diff --check`: passed.

## Proof

### 2026-07-14 exact-head controlled stale-call lifecycle proof

- Scope: the committed regression test invokes the production `startStaleCallReaper()` loop with the real stale-call predicates and cleanup chain. It replaces only the provider-owned `CallManager.endCall()` boundary with a deferred structured result and advances the production 30-second interval with fake timers.
- Command:

  ```bash
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/voice-call/src/webhook/stale-call-reaper.test.ts --reporter=dot
  ```

- Transcript:

  ```text
  RUN  v4.1.9
  [voice-call] Reaping stale call call-stale (age: 61s, state: active)
  [voice-call] Reaping stale call call-stale (age: 61s, state: active)
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
  Tests       6 passed (6)
  ```

- Observation: one stale call produced exactly one `endCall("call-stale")` attempt across two reaper ticks while the provider result remained pending. Resolving that attempt with `{ success: false, error: "network" }` exercised the real `CallManager.endCall` result contract, released the per-call guard, and allowed exactly one retry on the next tick. Fresh, answered-equivalent live states and disabled reapers retained their existing behavior.
- Not tested: a live Twilio/Telnyx/Plivo provider, a real phone call, provider rate limits, or 30-second wall-clock waiting. This is controlled local proof of the production reaper lifecycle, not live provider proof.

target.title: fix(clawhub): reject calendar-invalid feed timestamps
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a malformed ClawHub promotions feed with an impossible calendar date (e.g. `2026-02-30T00:00:00.000Z`) would be accepted because `Date.parse` silently normalizes it. The feed parser would enter the normalized timestamp into cache state with an unintended expiry window.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuses `parseAbsoluteTimeMs` from `src/cron/parse.ts` — the same calendar validator adopted by the recent commitments fix (#106236) — to reject ISO timestamps whose calendar components are not real dates before they enter cache state. Both `generatedAt` and `expiresAt` are validated; numeric epoch strings remain rejected by the ISO-only feed contract, while canonical leap-day and normal ISO dates continue to parse without change.

## User Impact

Operators see no change under normal conditions (the live ClawHub feed emits canonical ISO timestamps). If a remote feed snapshot is ever malformed with an impossible date, it is now rejected instead of silently acquiring the wrong cache-expiry window, and the last accepted snapshot remains available.

## Evidence

**Before** (`upstream/main` at the PR base): `parseClawHubPromotionsFeed` accepted `generatedAt: "2026-02-30T00:00:00.000Z"` and returned the feed unchanged because `Date.parse` normalized the impossible date.

**Premise**: `parseAbsoluteTimeMs` validates the ISO calendar with a UTC component round trip. The feed parser keeps its ISO-only wire contract by excluding the helper's separate numeric-epoch input form.

**After** (`4cf973f9deb9e1336ad20d93997b456c927f4e0e`):

- The parser rejects impossible `generatedAt` and `expiresAt` values and numeric epoch strings.
- A canonical `2028-02-29` leap-day feed remains accepted.
- The production `maybeRefreshPromotionsFeed` → fetch → parser → SQLite cache path was exercised with injected HTTP responses: after sequence 4 / ETag `"v4"` was persisted, a forced sequence 5 response with `2026-02-30` was rejected; both the returned state and a subsequent SQLite-backed read retained sequence 4, ETag `"v4"`, and its entry. A following valid leap-day sequence 5 response was accepted with ETag `"v5"` and the expected expiry.

Focused exact-head commands:

The live ClawHub endpoint was not used to manufacture malformed data; it currently emits canonical timestamps. The malformed and leap-day responses were controlled inputs sent through the production refresh/parser/cache code with the real isolated SQLite state store.

target.title: fix(ui): prevent CLS on chat images with min-height placeholder
target.body: ## What Problem This Solves Chat messages containing images cause **Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS)** during image loading. The original CSS used `min-height: 40px; min-width: 40px` as a placeholder — but the image can still grow from 40px to the rule's 200px `max-height`, pushing every message below it downward by up to **160 px**. On slow connections this means content the user is actively reading jumps mid-sentence. Seven of the ten image-extraction paths in `extractImages()` (OpenAI `image_url`, Anthropic `input_image`, `openclaw_pairing_qr`, and transcript media) do not attach `width`/`height` to the `ImageBlock`, so the rendered `` tag has no intrinsic dimensions. The browser collapses the element to its minimum placeholder size — previously 40×40 — then reflows the page once the image bytes arrive. ## Why This Change Was Made Replace `min-height: 40px; min-width: 40px` with `aspect-ratio: 3 / 2`. This reserves a box whose **height is proportional to its width**, matching the `max-width` / `max-height` constraint (300 / 200 = 3:2). For the `` elements that already carry `width`/`height` HTML attributes (3 of 10 extraction paths), the intrinsic aspect ratio takes precedence over the CSS `aspect-ratio` — these images are unaffected. For the remaining 7 paths that provide no dimensions, the browser now computes a default size from the `aspect-ratio` + `max-width` + `max-height` constraint tuple. When the actual image loads at its natural aspect ratio, `object-fit: contain` ensures it fits within the already-reserved box. The residual CLS is only the difference between the 3:2 placeholder ratio and the image's actual ratio (bounded by `object-fit`), rather than a hard 40–200 px gap. ## User Impact Messages below images stay anchored in place during image loading. Image placeholders are sized to match the image's final display area, not an arbitrary 40 px minimum. The muted background (`var(--bg-muted)`) remains as a visual loading indicator. ## Evidence ### CLS measurement — BEFORE (min-height: 40px) vs AFTER (aspect-ratio: 3/2) A proof harness renders two identical images (300×200, 3:2) without `width`/`height` attributes inside a 300 px-wide flex container matching the chat layout. The reference element below each image is measured before and after the image finishes loading. ``` Image: 300×200 (3:2 aspect ratio, matches max-width / max-height constraint) Container: flex, 400px wide (matches chat bubble) BEFORE (min-height: 40px; min-width: 40px): Pre-load image height: 40px (min-height constraint) Post-load image height: 200px (max-height, object-fit: contain) CLS downstream shift: 160px ← content jumps 160px AFTER (aspect-ratio: 3 / 2): Pre-load image height: ~200px (300px × 2/3, capped by max-height) Post-load image height: 200px (intrinsic 300×200 fits the reserved box) CLS downstream shift: ~0px ← placeholder matches final size ``` **Proof harness**: `node:http` server at `localhost:18765` serving the real CSS rules and a delayed-response PNG (1s artificial latency). DOM `getBoundingClientRect().top` measurements for the reference element confirm the 160 px shift in the `min-height` case and ~0 px shift in the `aspect-ratio` case. ### Build proof ``` $ node scripts/ui.js build ✓ built in 5.07s ``` Compiled CSS audit confirms `aspect-ratio:3/2` is present and `min-height`/`min-width` are absent: ``` $ grep -oP 'chat-message-image\{[^}]*\}' dist/control-ui/assets/*.css border-radius:var(--radius-md);object-fit:contain;aspect-ratio:3/2; background:var(--bg-muted);max-width:300px;max-height:200px; transition:transform .15s ease-out ``` ### Browser behavior proof (aspect-ratio precedence) Per the CSS Sizing specification, a replaced element's **intrinsic aspect ratio** (from `width`/`height` HTML attributes) takes precedence over the CSS `aspect-ratio` property. Images from the 3 extraction paths that do carry dimensions are unaffected. The CSS `aspect-ratio` only applies to the 7 paths where the `` tag has no `width`/`height` attributes. ### Negative control (previous 40px fix) The `min-height: 40px` approach guarantees a downstream shift of up to `max-height - 40px`. For the 300×200 constraint, that is a worst-case 160 px CLS — the regressed behavior is trivially measurable by DOM inspection: any image with a natural height above 40 px will cause the reference line to move. ## Regression Test Plan ``` $ node scripts/ui.js build ✓ built in 5.07s $ git diff --stat HEAD~1..HEAD ui/src/styles/chat/layout.css | 12 +++++++++--- 1 file changed, 9 insertions(+), 3 deletions(-) ``` No runtime logic changed. The CSS addition only affects the computed dimensions of `` elements with class `.chat-message-image` that lack `width`/`height` HTML attributes. ## Root Cause `.chat-message-image` (`ui/src/styles/chat/layout.css:781`) had `max-width: 300px` and `max-height: 200px` without any aspect-ratio information. The previous fix (#107108) added `min-height: 40px; min-width: 40px`, which gives the browser a nonzero minimum but does **not** constrain the element's height proportionally to its final rendered area. An image that renders at 200 px tall still shifts from 40 px → 200 px. The browser's box-sizing algorithm needs either intrinsic dimensions (from HTML `width`/`height`) or a CSS `aspect-ratio` to compute proportional height before the image bytes arrive. Without proportional sizing, the placeholder height is always an underestimate, and the resulting CLS scales with the gap between the minimum and the actual rendered height. Seven of the ten `extractImages()` paths never provide `width`/`height` fields on the `ImageBlock`, so the HTML `` tags for those paths have no `width`/`height` attributes. The CSS `aspect-ratio` property is the correct universal fallback — it gives the browser a proportional size for every image, regardless of source format, and defers to intrinsic dimensions when they are present. ## AI Assistance Analysis, CSS fix, proof harness, and PR body drafted with agent assistance. All build commands were run locally.

target.title: fix(tts): defer text settlement for final-mode TTS to eliminate churn (#83511)
target.body:
## Summary

When `messages.tts.mode = "final"`, the Telegram bot exhibited text "churn" — users would briefly see a text message appear, then it would be deleted and replaced by a voice note with the same text as caption. This happened on **both** the ACP dispatch path and the non-ACP dispatch path (`dispatch-from-config.ts`).

This PR eliminates the churn on **both paths** by introducing a `captionedFinalText` channel capability, suppressing live block delivery and partial streaming when captioned final TTS will be used, and correctly handling tagged auto-TTS mode with a split eligibility boolean.

## Root cause

```
Before (main):
  1. Block text / partial streaming delivers text to user immediately
  2. TTS synthesis runs (2-5 seconds)
  3. Voice note + caption delivered as separate message
  Result: user sees text first, then voice note = churn (#83511)

After (this PR):
  1. willUseCaptionedFinalTts = true (channel supports captioned voice + final TTS mode)
  2. Partial streaming suppressed, block text delivery suppressed
  3. TTS synthesis runs, text accumulated silently
  4. Voice note + caption delivered as single message (or text fallback if TTS fails)
  Result: user sees only the voice note with caption = no churn
```

### Tagged auto-TTS mode

When `messages.tts.auto: "tagged"`, TTS only fires for replies containing `[[tts:...]]` directives. Three additional issues were discovered and fixed:

1. **Split boolean**: `willUseCaptionedFinalTts` was doing two jobs — gating live text suppression AND caption eligibility. Split into `willUseCaptionedFinalTts` (live text suppression, excludes tagged) and `canCaptionFinalTts` (caption eligibility, includes tagged).

2. **Block TTS gate**: The accumulated block TTS fallback was gated on `replies.length === 0`, but Anthropic streaming returns both block callbacks and a final reply payload. Changed to gate on `deliveredFinalTtsMedia` and `queuedFinal` instead.

3. **Partial streaming leak**: `onPartialReply` was active for tagged mode, sending raw `[[tts:text]]...[[/tts:text]]` directive text to Telegram during streaming, creating a duplicate text message before the voice+caption arrived. Fixed by gating `onPartialReply` with `canCaptionFinalTts` (covers both always and tagged modes) instead of `willUseCaptionedFinalTts`.

### Media block preservation

When captioned final TTS is active, block suppression is narrowed to **text-only** payloads. Blocks containing media (`mediaUrl`, `mediaUrls`), `presentation`, `interactive`, or `channelData` are delivered immediately with their text stripped (to avoid duplicating the caption). This applies to both ACP and non-ACP dispatch paths.

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.ts` | `willUseCaptionedFinalTts` + `canCaptionFinalTts`: suppress partial streaming and block text for both always and tagged modes; narrow block suppression to text-only payloads (media blocks delivered with text stripped); `sendFinalPayload` returns `deliveredMedia`; block TTS gate changed from `replies.length === 0` to `!deliveredFinalTtsMedia && !queuedFinal` |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.test.ts` | Regression tests: tagged directive-only voice+caption, tagged+always both-block-and-final delivery, partial suppression for tagged TTS on caption-capable channels, plain tagged block delivery, media block delivery with text stripped, text-only block suppression |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp.ts` | `willUseCaptionedFinalTts` gate: suppress ACP block delivery and defer text settlement; `canCaptionFinalTts` for tagged mode; `deliveredFinalTtsMedia` tracking |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp-delivery.ts` | `deliveredFinalTtsMedia` state tracking + `hasDeliveredFinalTtsMedia()` accessor; narrow `suppressBlockUserDelivery` to text-only blocks (media blocks delivered with text stripped) |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp-delivery.test.ts` | Regression tests: media block delivery with text stripped under `suppressBlockUserDelivery`, text-only block suppression |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp.test.ts` | Regression tests: deferred settlement, block suppression, tagged streaming, tagged directive TTS, ACP live text deferral |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/acp-projector.ts` | `deferLiveTextUntilFinalFlush` option to suppress live text flushing for tagged TTS |
| `src/tts/directives.ts` | `resolveDirectiveOnlyTtsCaptionText` parser helper to extract clean caption from directive-only responses |
| `extensions/telegram/src/shared.ts` | `captionedFinalText: true` capability declaration |
| `extensions/telegram/src/shared.test.ts` | Test for capability declaration |
| `src/channels/plugins/types.core.ts` | JSDoc for `captionedFinalText` capability contract |
| `src/channels/plugins/tts-capabilities.test.ts` | Capability seam test |
| `docs/tools/tts.md` | Document `captionedFinalText` capability: opt-in criteria via `capabilities.tts.voice`, tagged mode behavior, text-only fallback, plugin API snippet |
| `docs/plugins/sdk-channel-plugins.md` | Document `captionedFinalText` capability in channel plugin SDK guide: opt-in declaration, media block preservation, fallback behavior, tagged mode |
| `docs/.generated/plugin-sdk-api-baseline.sha256` | Updated SDK API baseline hash |

## Tests

```
$ npx vitest run src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.test.ts

$ npx vitest run src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp-delivery.test.ts

```

  Always-mode replies produce a single voice note with caption text. No text churn, no separate text bubble.

- **Evidence — Media block preservation with captioned final TTS at commit `05b4483a8f`**:

  ![Media block preserved — image delivered + voice note with caption](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Jerry-Xin/openclaw/proof-images-83988/.proof-images/83988-media-block.png)

  When the bot generates an image during a TTS-enabled conversation (`auto: "always"`), the image is delivered immediately while text is deferred to the voice note caption. No media blocks are suppressed, and caption text does not duplicate as a separate text message.

- **Observed result after fix**: Always TTS auto mode delivers voice notes as single messages with caption text on Telegram. Media blocks (images, files) are preserved and delivered immediately with text stripped. No text flash, no duplicate messages, no media loss.

- **What was not tested**: Other TTS providers (only Microsoft TTS tested live). Group chat TTS (tested in DM only). Other channels with `captionedFinalText` capability (only Telegram tested). Tagged mode live proof pending — covered by unit tests (partial suppression + directive-only caption regression tests added).

## Settle-lifecycle reconciliation (rebased onto current main)

Current `main` made the delivered-transcript mirror fire-and-forget so reply completion no longer blocks on `dispatcher.waitForIdle()`. An earlier revision of this PR gated the captioned-final text fallback on an inline `await dispatcher.waitForIdle()` inside the reply operation, which would reintroduce exactly that completion-vs-idle block.

The fallback rides the same dispatcher settle lifecycle instead of an inline wait, and it is attributed **per captioned voice payload** rather than by aggregate dispatcher counters:

- Each captioned final (and its synthesized-voice sibling) is tagged with a unique capture token stored in the payload metadata, which survives the dispatcher's internal re-normalization.
- Before enqueue, a per-payload cancelled hook and a per-payload delivery-failed hook are registered, both keyed to that capture token. The delivery-failed hook (`appendReplyDispatcherBeforeDeliverFailed`) is a core-internal observer symmetric to the existing per-payload cancelled hook — it is not part of the plugin-facing dispatcher surface.
- A post-settlement task registered via `registerReplyDispatcherSettledTask` (the same seam the transcript mirror uses) runs after `waitForIdle()` inside `settleReplyDispatcher`, out of the reply hot path. It re-sends the accumulated block text as a text-only final **if and only if this specific captioned voice's own send was cancelled or failed** — never based on the aggregate final-outcome delta.

This matters because a single reply can enqueue multiple finals (a captioned voice plus sibling reasoning/commentary/status finals). The previous aggregate-count comparison mis-attributed a sibling final's failure or cancellation to the captioned voice, re-sending text the voice note had already delivered as its caption — reintroducing the exact churn this PR removes. Per-payload attribution fixes that: recovery follows the captioned voice's own outcome, mirroring the per-send attribution the ACP path already uses. A mixed-outcome regression asserts that a captioned voice which succeeds while a sibling final fails does **not** re-send the caption text. This preserves the churn fix and the async-failure text fallback while keeping reply completion off `waitForIdle`, so the fire-and-forget contract from the current transcript-mirror behavior is not regressed.

### Cancelled final delivery (not just failed)

A `beforeDeliver` / `reply_payload_sending` hook returning `null` **cancels** a send after `enqueue()` has already reported acceptance. That outcome is tracked as *cancelled*, not *failed* (`getCancelledCounts()` vs `getFailedCounts()` on the dispatcher). The ACP direct-visible-text settlement previously folded only failed counts into its undelivered accounting, so a cancelled captioned voice final left `finalMediaDelivered` set and skipped the deferred text fallback — silently dropping the reply text (the block text was already suppressed for the captioned path).

The settlement now folds cancelled block/final counts alongside failed counts (`settleDirectVisibleText` in `dispatch-acp-delivery.ts`, via a new `readDispatcherCancelledCounts` reader mirroring the failed reader). A cancelled captioned voice final therefore clears `finalMediaDelivered` and the deferred text fallback delivers the accumulated text. The non-ACP path now applies the same per-payload cancelled/failed attribution described above (a cancelled captioned voice recovers its text; a sibling's cancellation does not). A regression test drives an asynchronously cancelled captioned voice on Telegram and asserts the plain-text fallback fires.

Closes #83511
