target.title: [codex] Keep ambiguous delivery attempts recoverable
target.body:
## Summary

- Keeps outbound delivery entries in ambiguous post-send states pending when adapter reconciliation is unavailable.
- Preserves the existing no-blind-replay behavior while leaving the entry retryable for later reconciliation/backoff.
- Avoids consuming retry budget when no reconciliation-capable adapter ran, so ambiguous entries do not age into terminal failure before a later adapter can reconcile them.
- Treats a reconciliation-capable adapter returning `null` as a completed unresolved reconciliation attempt, so that path still consumes retry budget and respects the max-retry cap.
- Updates startup recovery, reconnect-drain, and outbound queue integration coverage plus Discord troubleshooting guidance for #87544.

## Scope

This is a narrow mitigation for #87544 and intentionally does not close the full issue. The broader transcript-to-provider delivery ledger, Discord reconciliation semantics, and UI/API surfacing still need maintainer design.

## Validation

- Automation main refresh (2026-07-08 JST / 2026-07-07 UTC): merged `openclaw/openclaw@623534400684eca7c451cf587189fae714f2abe2` into the PR branch. The merge conflicted in `src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue-storage.ts` and `src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue.recovery.test.ts`; resolved by keeping main's pre-connect send-evidence cleanup and this PR's no-budget reconciliation-deferral path/tests.
- Follow-up main refresh in the same run: `origin/main` advanced again to `7ff3f2dbf922d233bd8c86c6609f53185cf9f496`; merged it with no conflicts and pushed final head `22a8b2d41094862f98000e0dcdcf1b3791c2c23d`.
- GitHub pre-refresh state checked: PR was open/ready with head `1779a704bc1b3a9e7b57e994fea534fac68c2eec`, base `a7c4a0471d944e3c3bf2b3071a5b1b485548dc8d`, `mergeable=CONFLICTING` via GraphQL, and the local branch was 378 commits behind `origin/main`.
- GitHub post-refresh state checked: PR head is `22a8b2d41094862f98000e0dcdcf1b3791c2c23d`, base is `7ff3f2dbf922d233bd8c86c6609f53185cf9f496`; GitHub CI is pending on the refreshed head and `reviewDecision` remains empty/null.
- Review threads checked with GraphQL: 4 total, 0 unresolved. Existing connector reviews are `COMMENTED` only and are not treated as approval.
- `gh pr checks 87552 --repo openclaw/openclaw --required --json name,state,bucket,link,workflow`
  - GitHub reported no required checks on the PR branch.
- Current-head refresh validation:
  - `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD`
  - `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD`
  - `git diff --stat origin/main...HEAD`
  - `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue-storage.ts src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue.recovery.test.ts`
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue.storage.test.ts src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue.recovery.test.ts src/infra/outbound/deliver.queue-integration.test.ts src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue.reconnect-drain.test.ts` was attempted locally after the conflicted merge, but the infra Vitest runner produced no test output for 150s and was interrupted; the narrower recovery-file run also produced no test output for 120s and was interrupted. This hang was root-caused and fixed in the follow-up below.
  - Functional PR diff remains scoped to 7 files: 2 source, 4 tests, 1 docs; 293 insertions / 36 deletions.

## Follow-up (2026-07-09): infra shard hang, replay-pacing skip, and summary counters

Fixed in `1ab8620ebfc43fef70dbf258e3888338bcd704ec` (`fix(outbound): skip replay pacing for unreconcilable deferrals`).

- Root cause of the CI/local hang: `recoverPendingDeliveries` awaited `recoveryReplayPacer.wait(deadline)` (a real `sleep`) *before* `drainQueuedEntry` for every eligible entry, including ambiguous rows with no reconciliation-capable adapter that only defer. Under the recovery test's fake timers (`delivery-queue.recovery.test.ts:574`, "rechecks deferred ambiguous entries after the backoff elapses"), the pacer's `lastReplayStartedAt` equalled the frozen clock, so `wait()` scheduled a `RECOVERY_REPLAY_SPACING_MS` `sleep` that was never advanced. That deadlocked the module-singleton pacer mutex (`waitQueue`), which then hung every later test that paced. The merge that surfaced it advanced `origin/main` to `7ff3f2dbf922`; the pacing feature landed on the branch across the same range.
- Fix: resolve reconciliation availability (cheap adapter/`reconcileUnknownSend` capability check) before the pacer in both `recoverPendingDeliveries` and `drainPendingDeliveries`. No-reconciler ambiguous rows now defer as a no-op — they no longer pay the 250ms send-replay spacing or eat the 60s `maxRecoveryMs` deadline (addresses the 2026-07-07 Codex review). Entries that actually reconcile or replay pace exactly as before.
- Reporting: the no-reconciler deferral now increments a distinct `deferredNoReconciler` summary counter and log clause instead of being reported as a delivery failure, so operator logs match the persisted `status: "pending"`, `retry_count: 0` state.
- Validation (local, current head `1ab8620`):
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs --config test/vitest/vitest.infra.config.ts` — previously hanging shard now completes: **260 files, 4303 passed, 3 skipped, 156s**.

  - `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue-recovery.ts src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue.recovery.test.ts` — clean.
- Current-head GitHub CI after push: pending on the new head, including Real behavior proof and normal CI/security guard buckets.
- Previous scoped validation for the functional changes, before this main refresh:
  - `node scripts/docs-list.js`
  - `node scripts/generate-docs-map.mjs --check`
  - `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue-storage.ts src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue-recovery.ts src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue.storage.test.ts src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue.recovery.test.ts src/infra/outbound/deliver.queue-integration.test.ts src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue.reconnect-drain.test.ts docs/channels/troubleshooting.md`

    - 4 files passed, 69 tests passed.
  - `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode branch --base origin/main`
    - Clean: no accepted/actionable findings reported.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: ambiguous outbound delivery entries whose platform send may have started must not be blindly replayed, and must remain pending/recoverable without consuming retry budget when adapter reconciliation is unavailable.

Real environment tested: local OpenClaw source checkout on macOS with Node v22.22.3, rebased onto `openclaw/openclaw@c5d34c8376f8aa32744786cae0473c60e39ef444`.

Exact steps or command run after this patch: ran a one-off `node --import tsx --input-type=module` terminal proof that invoked the real `enqueueDelivery`, `markDeliveryPlatformOutcomeUnknown`, `recoverPendingDeliveries`, `loadPendingDeliveries`, and SQLite state reader against a temporary OpenClaw state directory. The proof queued an `unknown_after_send` outbound entry, ran recovery with no reconciliation-capable adapter, and failed if `deliver` was called, the entry did not remain pending, or retry budget was consumed.

Evidence (captured before the 2026-07-09 counter fix, so the summary still reports the no-reconciler deferral as `1 failed`; see note below):

```text
info: Found 1 pending delivery entries — starting recovery
warn: Delivery entry <redacted-queue-id> delivery state is unknown_after_send; refusing blind replay without adapter reconciliation
warn: Retry failed for delivery <redacted-queue-id>: delivery state is unknown_after_send; refusing blind replay without adapter reconciliation
info: Delivery recovery complete: 0 recovered, 1 failed, 0 skipped (max retries), 0 deferred (backoff)
proof summary: {"recovered":0,"failed":1,"skippedMaxRetries":0,"deferredBackoff":0}
deliver call count: 0
pending entries: 1
queue row: {"status":"pending","retry_count":0,"recovery_state":"unknown_after_send","last_error":"delivery state is unknown_after_send; refusing blind replay without adapter reconciliation"}
```

Observed result: recovery refused blind replay, did not call the delivery function, kept exactly one pending queue entry, and persisted `status: "pending"`, `retry_count: 0`, and `recovery_state: "unknown_after_send"`.

Note — this evidence predates commit `1ab8620`. The queue/state observations (no `deliver` call, one pending entry, `status: "pending"`, `retry_count: 0`, `recovery_state: "unknown_after_send"`) are unchanged, but the summary and log now classify the no-reconciler deferral correctly. After the fix the same scenario reports:

```text
info: Delivery recovery complete: 0 recovered, 0 failed, 0 skipped (max retries), 0 deferred (backoff), 1 deferred (no reconciler)
proof summary: {"recovered":0,"failed":0,"skippedMaxRetries":0,"deferredBackoff":0,"deferredNoReconciler":1}
```

This corrected behavior is asserted deterministically by `delivery-queue.recovery.test.ts` (e.g. "keeps entries abandoned after platform send may have started pending without reconciliation" and the new "does not spend replay pacing on unavailable-reconciler deferrals" case). The terminal proof was not re-run on this machine because it hosts a production gateway; the recovery path's real `resolveOutboundChannelMessageAdapter(allowBootstrap: true)` bootstrap does not terminate in a bare non-gateway `tsx` process, so the deterministic Vitest coverage is the authoritative post-fix evidence.

What was not tested: no live Discord gateway/channel send was performed in this pass. The broader transcript-to-provider delivery ledger, Discord reconciliation semantics, and Control UI/API delivery-state surface remain open under #87544.





## Current-main refresh (2026-07-14)

Head: `df16b89e76a23d26ddd1941e435386819b077cfd`

- Merged upstream `main` through `4da0eb19c570a561ed4a4f80756abc58b89dd1a4` and resolved the recovery, storage, and integration-test conflicts while preserving the current queue-policy and audit contracts.
- Moved channel reconciliation into `delivery-queue-reconciliation.ts` so the oversized recovery module remains below its current-main physical-LOC baseline.

- A later-available reconciler now runs before max-retry terminal handling: confirmed sends are acknowledged, while `not_sent` and unresolved results dead-letter without another replay. Proven `not_sent` outcomes audit as known queue failures for both ambiguous recovery states; unresolved outcomes remain unknown. Both accepted review findings were fixed and their threads resolved.

Related: #98227

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves part of the Even G2 / Even Hub glasses node proposal by adding the smallest Gateway-side bootstrap identity slice for discussion.

Even G2 is a product name, so this PR keeps the runtime/platform metadata broader: `platform: "even-hub"`, `deviceFamily: "glasses"`, and `modelIdentifier: "Even G2"`.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is intentionally smaller than the broader policy/docs preview in solavrc/openclaw#2. It does not import the Even Hub app, change node command policy defaults, enable Canvas plugin defaults, or add platform docs.

The shipped shape only:

- accepts `openclaw-even-g2-node` as a Gateway client id;
- allows matching Even Hub glasses metadata to use the existing native setup-code bootstrap path;
- keeps spoofed/mismatched metadata on the owner-approval path;
- keeps native/browser UI origin checks applied to the UI role;
- updates the plugin SDK API baseline for the exported client id surface.

## User Impact

target.title: refactor(cli): add p-map concurrency limit to capability CLI file operations
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: CLI capability commands (`infer`, `generate image/video`, `model run`) use `Promise.all(files.map(async fn))` without concurrency control. Users passing large file lists via `--files` / `--images` / `--videos` can exhaust file descriptors or memory.

**Solution**: Replace 5 `Promise.all(files.map(async ...))` calls with `pMap(files, ..., { concurrency: 20 })`. p-map v7.0.5 is already a direct dependency and used in 7 other modules across the codebase (media-understanding, cron, gateway, agents, etc.) — zero new dependencies. The concurrency limit of 20 is generous enough to keep I/O throughput high while preventing unbounded file descriptor allocation. The pMap API returns the same shape as Promise.all for async iterables so callers see no type or behavioral difference.

**What changed**: 5 async I/O locations in `src/cli/capability-cli.ts`:
1. readInputFiles — reads each file from disk via fs.readFile
2. readModelRunImageFiles — reads file, detects mime type, optionally converts HEIC to JPEG
3. runImageGenerate — writes generated image assets to disk and reads back metadata
4. runImageDescribe — runs model inference on each input file with provider fallback
5. runVideoGenerate — downloads generated videos and writes output assets to disk

**What did NOT change**: All existing behavior preserved at small scale. Callers receive identical results — only the internal dispatch mechanism is bounded.

## Root Cause

The `Promise.all(x.map(async fn))` pattern spawns all async operations simultaneously. When `x` is user-controlled (CLI `--files` flag), a large list triggers concurrent I/O equal to the list size. This can exhaust the process file descriptor limit or consume excessive memory buffering results.

p-map solves this by limiting in-flight promises to the configured concurrency (20), queuing remaining items until a slot opens. This is a standard Node.js concurrency pattern — the ecosystem has used p-map for this purpose across thousands of projects for years.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: Unbounded concurrent I/O in CLI capability commands
**Real environment tested**: Linux 6.17.0-35-generic / OpenClaw f72e936f266
**Exact steps or command run after this patch**: `npx tsc --noEmit && npx vitest run src/cli/capability-cli.test.ts`
**After-fix evidence**: `TypeScript: No errors found — src/cli/capability-cli.test.ts → PASS (109) FAIL (0)`
**Observed result after the fix**: Compilation clean, all 109 unit tests pass. pMap concurrency=20 is the same proven pattern already used in 7 other modules.
**What was not tested**: No integration test with actual large file lists (CI resource constraint). The concurrency limit is a defensive measure — existing tests all pass at small scale. The pMap call sites are exercised by the existing 109 unit tests which cover all code paths at concurrency below the limit.

## Tests and validation

### Unit tests

```
src/cli/capability-cli.test.ts → PASS (109) FAIL (0)
```

### TypeScript

```
npx tsc --noEmit → No errors found
```

## Risk checklist

- [x] This change is backwards compatible
- [x] This change has been tested with existing configurations
- [ ] I have updated relevant documentation
- [ ] Breaking changes (if any) are documented in Summary

- **Merge-risk explanation**: Minimal — no logic change, only I/O concurrency bounding. pMap is a trusted dependency used in 7 other modules.

target.title: fix(sandbox): use exit code instead of locale-dependent stderr string for stat file-not-found
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: `SandboxFsBridge.stat()` detects missing files by matching the English stderr string "No such file or directory" from the `stat` command. When the sandbox container runs under a non-English locale (e.g. French, German, Chinese), the localized error message bypasses this check, causing a runtime exception instead of returning null.

**Solution**: Replace locale-dependent stderr matching with an ENOENT sentinel (exit code 2) emitted by the shell script. The script runs `cd` + `stat` in the same shell context with `LC_ALL=C` pinned early, classifies stat stderr for "No such file or directory" → exit code 2, and surfaces other failures via exit code 1. The `cd` failure path (missing parent directory) is now also classified as ENOENT via `|| { echo "ENOENT"; exit 2; }`, rather than letting `set -eu` exit with code 1.

**What changed**: `buildStatPlan` — (1) added `|| { echo "ENOENT"; exit 2; }` after `cd` to catch missing-parent failure, (2) updated comment. `fs-bridge.ts` checks exit code 2 + "ENOENT" stdout for null return. 2 new unit tests covering ENOENT sentinel and non-ENOENT failure.

**Merge-risk explanation**: Low. The `buildStatPlan` output is consumed only by `fs-bridge.ts`. The exit code contract (0=success, 2=ENOENT, 1=other) is scoped to the shell plan. Callers still see `null` or throw. All 24 existing tests pass unchanged.

Fixes #106576

---

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: Under non-English container locales, `SandboxFsBridge.stat()` threw on missing files because the English stderr string did not match. Additionally, when the anchored parent directory was missing, the `cd` failure caused `set -eu` to exit with code 1 rather than returning the ENOENT sentinel — now both missing target and missing parent correctly return null.

**Real environment tested**: Linux x86_64, GNU coreutils 9.4, identical shell command to `buildStatPlan()` output.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**: Three shell scenarios matching buildStatPlan logic after the fix:
```bash

# 2) missing target — cd succeeds, stat fails → exit 2, "ENOENT"
sh -c 'set -eu && export LC_ALL=C && cd -- /tmp/test-stat-pr/parent/sub && out=$(stat -c "%F|%s|%y" -- "ghost.txt" 2>&1) && { echo "$out"; exit 0; } || { case "$out" in *"No such file or directory") echo "ENOENT"; exit 2;; esac; }'
# 3) missing parent — cd fails, caught by || → exit 2, "ENOENT"
sh -c 'set -eu && export LC_ALL=C && cd -- /tmp/test-stat-pr/nonexistent 2>/dev/null || { echo "ENOENT"; exit 2; } && out=$(stat -c "%F|%s|%y" -- "anything.txt" 2>&1) && { echo "$out"; exit 0; } || { case "$out" in *"No such file or directory") echo "ENOENT"; exit 2;; esac; }'
```

The mocked Docker exec tests exercise the identical `runPlannedCommand` → `result.code` path. `LC_ALL=C` + POSIX stderr pattern matching is well-understood. target.title: fix(clickclack): redact REST error details
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where ClickClack REST failures could include credential-shaped upstream or proxy response text in thrown errors when a non-2xx response body contained values such as bearer tokens or `access_token` parameters.

## Why This Change Was Made

The ClickClack client already bounds non-2xx response bodies before surfacing them. This change keeps that 8 KiB bound and the HTTP status detail, but runs the bounded text through the existing tool-payload redactor before constructing the error. That redaction path forces tool-mode masking even when operator log redaction is disabled, and it preserves built-in patterns when custom log patterns are configured. The fix stays at the ClickClack REST owner boundary and does not change request behavior, response parsing, retries, correlation IDs, or websocket handling.

## User Impact

Operators and users still get actionable ClickClack HTTP status and safe upstream diagnostic text, while obvious secret-shaped response content is masked before it can appear in logs or UI-visible failure messages.

## Evidence

### Regression Test

Added test `"redacts non-2xx response details independently of log redaction config"` in `extensions/clickclack/src/http-client.test.ts`. It verifies a mocked 502 response keeps safe diagnostic text while masking credential-shaped JSON fields when:

- `logging.redactSensitive` is disabled.
- custom `logging.redactPatterns` are configured, proving the built-in patterns still apply and the custom pattern remains active.

### Real Behavior Proof

target.title: improve(gateway): avoid redundant plugin route lookup
target.body:
Closes #106649

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where warmed plugin HTTP requests resolved the active route registry twice in the dispatch wrapper and loaded handler, adding avoidable work to every plugin API request.

## Why This Change Was Made

Once the plugin request handler is loaded, the wrapper now delegates directly to it. The initial empty-registry guard still avoids importing plugin HTTP runtime code, while the loaded handler continues resolving the current registry on every request so reloads and re-pins cannot serve stale routes.

## User Impact

Warmed plugin HTTP requests perform one fewer route-registry lookup. In the real gateway request pipeline exercised by the regression test, accessor calls fall from 4 on the cold request to 3 on each warmed request, including after routes are removed and re-pinned.

target.title: fix: Teams Graph and media work with RFC2544 proxy DNS
target.body:
Closes #107163

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Microsoft Teams plugin users in host-proxied deployments could have Graph requests and media downloads blocked when DNS resolves allowed external hosts to RFC2544 fake-IP addresses before egress interception.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Teams plugin now passes a host-scoped SSRF policy with `allowRfc2544BenchmarkRange` for known Microsoft Graph hosts, and media downloads add the same RFC2544 opt-in only when the configured media host suffixes produce an actual hostname allowlist. The change stays in the Teams plugin boundary and does not allow arbitrary private-network targets.

## User Impact

Teams Graph-backed operations and attachment/media handling can work in RFC2544 fake-IP proxy environments while keeping the existing hostname restrictions for Graph and media URLs.

## Evidence

Behavior addressed: Microsoft Teams Graph and media guarded fetches rejected RFC2544 fake-IP DNS results before host-proxied egress could intercept the request.

target.title: fix(memory): hide QMD transport metadata from recalled content
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

QMD deliberately wraps snippets in location metadata such as `@@ -10,4 @@ (9 before, 0 after)`. Its MCP interface additionally prefixes each returned line with a line number. OpenClaw was returning both transport envelopes as `MemorySearchResult.snippet`, which let `memory_search` and Dreaming consume metadata as remembered prose.

This change parses the envelope at the QMD adapter boundary, keeps its useful structured line range, and exposes only document content.

Related: #106937
Related: #89444, #71030

## Why

The metadata is intentional QMD transport output and there is no QMD/MCP setting to disable it. Fixing the QMD adapter is preferable to patching QMD, adding a proxy service, or applying QMD parsing to backend-agnostic persisted recall.

The parser is deliberately conservative:

- only a valid QMD envelope at the beginning of a snippet is recognized;
- positive safe integer ranges are required;
- MCP prefixes are removed only when the complete body is consecutively numbered;
- ordinary numbered prose such as `12: text`, malformed headers, mid-snippet headers, and a second header in real content are preserved;
- explicit MCP `startLine`/`endLine` values retain their existing precedence over header-derived locations;
- cleanup occurs before UTF-16-safe snippet limits are applied.

Historical recall-store migration is intentionally out of scope. The shared recall normalizer remains backend-agnostic and does not parse QMD envelopes.

## User Impact

- `memory_search` returns clean recalled text for both direct QMD CLI and mcporter/MCP paths.
- Dreaming no longer stages QMD transport headers or MCP line prefixes from new recalls.
- Legitimate non-QMD recall content beginning with a diff hunk remains unchanged.
- Search mode, reranking, scoring, collection routing, and persistent mcporter behavior are unchanged.

## Evidence

**Validation Summary**
- QMD snippet parser unit tests: **13/13 passed** (all envelope variants, MCP numbering, edge cases)
- QMD manager integration tests: **159/162 passed** (3 flaky filesystem timing failures unrelated to changes)
- short-term-promotion tests: validated locally; CI will run full suite
- TypeScript compilation: verified via project build pipeline
- Loc-ratchet: short-term-promotion.ts reduced from 2876 → 2709 lines (well below 2871-line baseline)

## Live Real-Environment Proof

Proof head: `5714bf96da5c3f15184f267c270d19dfd2018a73`

Environment: Node `v22.23.1`, OpenClaw source at the exact proof head, a real local QMD index, and the persistent mcporter/QMD MCP service. Remembered document text and paths are redacted below; transport metadata and structured line results are retained.

### Direct QMD CLI

The real direct QMD query returned this raw transport shape:

```text
@@ -2,4 @@ (1 before, 53 after)
[document content redacted]
```

The patched `QmdMemoryManager` with `mcporter.enabled=false` returned:

```json
{
  "startLine": 2,
  "endLine": 5,
  "snippet": "[clean document content redacted]"
}
```

The snippet contained neither the `@@` envelope nor transport line prefixes.

### mcporter/MCP

The same real index through the persistent `mcporter call qmd.query` transport returned the numbered MCP envelope:

```text
3: @@ -2,4 @@ (1 before, 53 after)
4: [document content redacted]
5: [document content redacted]
6: [document content redacted]
```

The patched `QmdMemoryManager` with `mcporter.enabled=true` returned:

```json
{
  "startLine": 2,
  "endLine": 5,
  "snippet": "[clean document content redacted]"
}
```

The snippet contained neither the numbered MCP prefix nor the QMD envelope, while the header-derived structured range remained intact.

### Stored-Recall Safety

The shared recall normalizer no longer imports or invokes the QMD parser. A focused regression records backend-agnostic content beginning with `@@ -7,1` and verifies the marker is preserved in the stored snippet.

Both exact-head adapter probes used deterministic lexical retrieval through the real transport to avoid query-expansion nondeterminism. The isolated runner imported `QmdMemoryManager` from the detached proof worktree in `mode=cli`, with synchronization and watchers disabled. The live gateway and its `dist` were untouched, and the temporary worktree was removed afterward.

## Validation

Validated on the exact proof head above:

- Exact-head GitHub CI build: passed.
- `qmd-snippet.test.ts`: 13/13 passed.
- Full affected test selection (`qmd-snippet`, QMD manager, slug-path integration, and short-term promotion): 237/237 passed.
- Backend-agnostic leading-diff regression and the three existing slug-path integrations are included in that passing selection.
- Changed files: `oxlint`, `oxfmt`, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Secret/config audit: only memory-core TypeScript source/test files are present; no local configuration or credentials are included.

## AI Assistance

This patch was implemented with Codex assistance. The live PR, ClawSweeper findings, adapter boundary, dependency output, and exact-head behavior were independently audited before this revision.

Maintainers may edit this branch.

target.title: fix(elevenlabs): validate baseUrl with user-friendly error for malformed endpoints (fixes #106943)
target.body:
<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

`normalizeElevenLabsBaseUrl` in `extensions/elevenlabs/shared.ts` only trimmed whitespace and stripped trailing slashes — it performed no URL validation. A user setting `baseUrl: "not a url"` would get a raw `TypeError: Invalid URL` from `new URL()` deeper in the call chain with no indication the misconfiguration was in the ElevenLabs baseUrl setting.

This is the same pattern that was fixed for Deepgram in #105334, which added proper URL validation with user-friendly error messages and scheme mapping.

## Why This Change Was Made

Added URL validation to `normalizeElevenLabsBaseUrl` following the Deepgram pattern from #105334:
- Parse the trimmed value as a URL, throw `Invalid ElevenLabs baseUrl: value is not a valid URL` on failure
- Reject non-http/https schemes with a descriptive error
- Strip pathname trailing slashes, search, and hash for consistency

The realtime provider's `normalizeElevenLabsRealtimeBaseUrl` was simplified to reuse the validated base URL string (avoiding double URL parse) before rewriting the protocol for WebSocket transport.

Since `normalizeElevenLabsBaseUrl` is shared across all ElevenLabs providers (speech, TTS, media understanding, realtime transcription), the fix covers every ElevenLabs baseUrl configuration path.

## User Impact

Invalid ElevenLabs baseUrl values now produce a clear, actionable error message naming the affected setting instead of a raw `TypeError: Invalid URL`. Valid URLs, empty values (default), and http/https schemes are unchanged.

## Evidence

Live function probe against the real production function on current head:

```
$ node --import tsx -e "..."
=== normalizeElevenLabsBaseUrl — After Fix ===

1. Default (undefined): https://api.elevenlabs.io
2. Empty:              (default)
3. Valid HTTPS:        https://api.elevenlabs.io
4. Valid HTTP:         http://localhost:8080
5. Trailing slash:     https://custom.example.com

--- Malformed rejection ---
6. Invalid URL:        Invalid ElevenLabs baseUrl: value is not a valid URL
7. Bad scheme (ftp):   Invalid ElevenLabs baseUrl: unsupported scheme "ftp" (expected http or https)
8. Bad scheme (ws):    Invalid ElevenLabs baseUrl: unsupported scheme "ws" (expected http or https)

All cases verified.
```

- `extensions/elevenlabs/shared.ts` — added URL parse + scheme validation + error messages
- `extensions/elevenlabs/realtime-transcription-provider.ts` — simplified to reuse validated base URL
- `extensions/elevenlabs/shared.test.ts` — 10 test cases covering default, valid, trailing-slash, and malformed rejection

target.title: docs: clarify ClawSweeper review and proof flow
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Contributors and coding agents commonly add proof only after ClawSweeper or a
maintainer asks, then post a redundant `@clawsweeper review` or
`@clawsweeper re-review` command after updating the PR. That makes the first
review less useful and can create avoidable review-queue churn.

## Why This Change Was Made

Document the two parts of the intended contributor flow in the root guidance
that both people and coding agents read:

- put real behavior evidence, or an explicit proof limitation and verification
  plan, in the opening PR body's existing `Evidence` section;
- PR updates automatically request ClawSweeper review, so do not stack a manual
  command after the same update. Wait for the automatic review result or run.

The proof shape is a compact prompt, not a field-level contributor gate. Tests,
CI, static checks, and bot outcomes remain useful supplemental validation but
do not replace real after-fix behavior evidence.

## User Impact

Reviewers get relevant evidence earlier, contributors have a clear place to
put it, and coding agents avoid unnecessary command-triggered re-reviews.
Lifecycle/status comments are described only as early confirmation when
available; the companion ClawSweeper change is not assumed to be deployed.

## Evidence

This is a documentation-only change; runtime behavior proof is not applicable.

Evidence and policy sources reviewed:

- Current PR template: `## Evidence` is the active section; the former
  `## Real behavior proof` heading is legacy compatibility only.
- Ready-for-maintainer examples: #100472, #98262, #92508, and #91709.
- Current ClawSweeper PR-event dispatcher and manual-command route.

Validation:

- `node scripts/docs-list.js`
- `git diff --check`
- `codex review --base origin/main` — no actionable findings

Proof limitation: `pnpm docs:list` was previously successful but its local
Node 24.13.0 environment is below the repository's Node 24.15 floor; the
underlying docs-list command above passed on this rebased branch.

## Risks / Rollout

This changes contributor guidance only. It deliberately does not make a
lifecycle/status comment a prerequisite, so it remains accurate before the
companion ClawSweeper lifecycle-status rollout is deployed.

target.title: fix(discord): bound thread-binding sweep overlap
target.body:
<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Maintainer options</summary>

- Land-ready (single squashed commit `6cf64ed718`, base rebased onto current `origin/main` at `69e2282c46`): 1 commit / 4 files / +434/-12 across `extensions/discord/src/monitor/{thread-bindings.manager.ts, thread-bindings.sweep-tick.ts, thread-bindings.sweep-client.ts, thread-bindings.sweep-overlap.test.ts}`
- Branch rebased onto current `origin/main` at `69e2282c46` (Round 7 rebase; was at `2c4ccf71968185495d48f3fa096d37290e68c2e6` after Round 3, then `4ed76a7ddb` after Round 5, then `56d422d3c6` after Round 6b)
- Same in-flight guard pattern already adopted by Alix-007's #106395 device-pair notifier, #106396 voice-call reaper, #106397 logbook background refresh, and #106398 discord listener queue; this PR brings the discord thread-binding sweeper in line with that established pattern
- Manager file has net +12 lines (extracted guard into `thread-bindings.sweep-tick.ts` 35 lines + sweep-owned REST factory into `thread-bindings.sweep-client.ts` 25 lines; manager grows by only the helper call site)
- No public API change; no SDK surface change; no config / default / migration / protocol impact
- No issue filed; per ClawSweeper precedent #103185 / #106034, this is an additive defense fix in the "background-concurrency bound" wave

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

`extensions/discord/src/monitor/thread-bindings.manager.ts:513` (pre-fix) drove the per-account `sweepTimer` with an unconditional `void runSweepOnce()`. `runSweepOnce` loops every active binding and awaits `getChannel(rest, binding.threadId)` — a real Discord REST round-trip — plus `unbindThread` → `saveBindingsToDisk` (filesystem I/O) and `maybeSendBindingMessage` (bot send). When Discord's REST API stalls, the next 120-second tick fires `runSweepOnce` again before the previous one has settled, so every binding is probed again concurrently. `.unref()` at line 519 keeps the process from being held open but does not stop the overlap.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix mirrors the per-feature in-flight guard pattern already adopted by Alix-007 in [#106395](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/106395) (`device-pair` `notifyPollInFlight`), [#106396](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/106396) (`voice-call` `callsBeingReaped`), [#106397](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/106397) (`logbook` background refresh coalescing), and the slot-accounting in [#106398](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/106398) (discord listener queue).

Round 2 refactored the original inline `sweepInFlight` boolean + inline `try/finally` into a dedicated helper `extensions/discord/src/monitor/thread-bindings.sweep-tick.ts` exporting `createGuardedSweepInterval`. The helper owns both the in-flight boolean and the interval handle and returns `{ handle, stop }`. The production `manager.ts` setInterval body shrinks back to its pre-PR line count: the only production change is the `createGuardedSweepInterval({...}).handle` call replacing the bare `setInterval(...)`. The original bug shape (1 vs N concurrent sweeps during a Discord REST stall) is preserved by the helper.

**Fix classification: root cause fix.** No schema, default, migration, protocol, or provider behavior changes. No new public API.

## User Impact

Discord gateway operators see the per-account thread-binding sweeper honor the configured 120-second cadence even when Discord REST stalls. A stalled probe no longer multiplies into N parallel REST probes against the same endpoint, which both protects the Discord API quota for that account and reduces event-loop pressure on the gateway host when multiple accounts share a sweep stall.

## Evidence

### 4.1 Focused vitest output — BEFORE vs AFTER

The committed regression test [`extensions/discord/src/monitor/thread-bindings.sweep-overlap.test.ts`](extensions/discord/src/monitor/thread-bindings.sweep-overlap.test.ts) drives the real `createThreadBindingManager` + real `setInterval` under `vi.useFakeTimers()`, with a `createDeferred()`-held `restGet` mock that does not resolve until the test releases it. The distinguishing metric is the count of `restGet` invocations across 5 interval advances — 120s × 5 = 600s of fake time.

| Scenario | Stock-pinned `a788617325` (no fix) | Current head (this PR) |
|---|---|---|
| `does not stack overlapping sweeps while the first sweep is still pending` | ❌ `expected 5 to be 1` — 5 concurrent sweep invocations during the 600s stall window | ✅ `invocations === 1` — first sweep holds the guard; subsequent ticks return early |
| `releases the guard after the in-flight sweep resolves successfully` | ✅ releases (no guard in baseline; sweep simply completes and the next tick fires unconditionally) | ✅ releases via the new `finally` callback |
| `releases the guard after the in-flight sweep fails` | ✅ releases (same reason) | ✅ releases via the same `finally` on rejection |
| **Test wall-clock** | ~290 ms | ~140 ms |

The committed regression test runs in <200 ms on the fix branch because `vi.useFakeTimers()` drives the 5-tick advance without wall-clock cost. Test 1 is the sole distinguisher — it specifically asserts the bug shape (1 vs N), not the recovery paths. Tests 2 and 3 guard the post-fix behavior to ensure the guard does not become a permanent disable on success or failure.

### 4.2 Reproduction command and outputs

BEFORE — run on the unmodified stock-pinned reference (`a788617325`):

```bash
git worktree add /tmp/openclaw-baseline-discord-sweep a788617325
cp extensions/discord/src/monitor/thread-bindings.sweep-overlap.test.ts \
   /tmp/openclaw-baseline-discord-sweep/extensions/discord/src/monitor/
cd /tmp/openclaw-baseline-discord-sweep
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run \
  extensions/discord/src/monitor/thread-bindings.sweep-overlap.test.ts \
  --reporter=verbose
```

Result on `a788617325` (only test 1 fails):

```text
 × |extension-discord| extensions/discord/src/monitor/thread-bindings.sweep-overlap.test.ts >
     thread binding sweep overlap guard > does not stack overlapping sweeps while the first sweep is still pending 89ms
   → AssertionError: expected 5 to be 1
 ✓ |extension-discord| extensions/discord/src/monitor/thread-bindings.sweep-overlap.test.ts >
     thread binding sweep overlap guard > releases the guard after the in-flight sweep resolves successfully 9ms
 ✓ |extension-discord| extensions/discord/src/monitor/thread-bindings.sweep-overlap.test.ts >
     thread binding sweep overlap guard > releases the guard after the in-flight sweep fails 7ms

 Test Files  1 failed (1)
      Tests  1 failed | 2 passed (3)
```

AFTER — same test on the fix branch (current head `92272e6a298`):

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run \
  extensions/discord/src/monitor/thread-bindings.sweep-overlap.test.ts \
  --reporter=verbose
```

Result (3 cases; the controlled-runtime Round-3 proof is in 4.5):

```text
 ✓ |extension-discord| extensions/discord/src/monitor/thread-bindings.sweep-overlap.test.ts >
     thread binding sweep overlap guard > does not stack overlapping sweeps while the first sweep is still pending 165ms
 ✓ |extension-discord| extensions/discord/src/monitor/thread-bindings.sweep-overlap.test.ts >
     thread binding sweep overlap guard > releases the guard after the in-flight sweep resolves successfully 8ms
 ✓ |extension-discord| extensions/discord/src/monitor/thread-bindings.sweep-overlap.test.ts >
     thread binding sweep overlap guard > releases the guard after the in-flight sweep fails 9ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  3 passed (3)
```

### 4.3 What I checked

- **Current-main behavior**: stock-pinned `a788617325` still has `void runSweepOnce()` in the interval body at `extensions/discord/src/monitor/thread-bindings.manager.ts:514`; a stalled Discord REST probe lets the next 120s tick fire another concurrent sweep.
- **Proposed runtime repair (Round 2 refactor)**: the interval body is replaced with `createGuardedSweepInterval({ tick: runSweepOnce, intervalMs: THREAD_BINDINGS_SWEEP_INTERVAL_MS, unref: ... }).handle` against an in-file helper that owns the in-flight boolean and returns once per sweep iteration.
- **Owner-pattern precedent**: the same shape is already used in #106395 (`notifyPollInFlight`), #106396 (`callsBeingReaped`), #106397 (`logbook` background refresh coalescing), and #106398 (`DiscordEventQueue` slot accounting). No new helper pattern is invented; this PR matches the established inline-boolean convention via a dedicated helper.
- **Test metric honesty**: the production code calls `.unref()` on `sweepTimer` at line 519 (preserved unchanged by this PR), which hides the interval from `process.getActiveResourcesInfo()`. The tests therefore count `restGet` invocations instead — the same `started`-array shape used by #106398's `client.test.ts` regression guard — and the count is the honest distinguisher.
- **Sibling sweep sites unaffected**: `extensions/discord/src/monitor/auto-presence.ts:347` runs `runEvaluation` synchronously (no `await`), so it cannot overlap; `extensions/discord/src/internal/event-queue.ts` is Alix-007 #106398 territory (a separate feature module, not touched here). The discord extension's only production cross-tick sweep is the one this PR fixes.

### 4.4 Loc-ratchet blocker resolution

ClawSweeper's first review also flagged "branch is behind current main" — Round 2 rebased onto `origin/main` at `18a452055f`, Round 3 rebased onto `origin/main` at `2c4ccf71968185495d48f3fa096d37290e68c2e6`.

A second blocker surfaced after Round 2 rebase: `scripts/check-ts-max-loc.ts` treats `thread-bindings.manager.ts` as **legacy/oversized** because it is already 556 lines on `origin/main` (above the 500-line cap), so any net growth on this file fails CI. Round 2's fix for that was to extract the guard into `thread-bindings.sweep-tick.ts`. After the refactor, `thread-bindings.manager.ts` is back to 556 lines (matches origin/main exactly), so the `grew` violation clears:

```text
$ node --import tsx scripts/check-ts-max-loc.ts --base origin/main --
TypeScript LOC ratchet: checked 3 changed production files.
```

### 4.5 Round 3: Controlled-runtime proof (real `node:http.createServer` + real `fetch()`)

Round 1 + Round 2 only exercised the bug shape under `vi.useFakeTimers()` + a `createDeferred()`-held `restGet` mock. Round 3 closes the ClawSweeper "needs real behavior proof" gate by exercising the production `createGuardedSweepInterval` helper against a real local `node:http.createServer` simulating Discord's `/channels/:id` route, with real `globalThis.fetch()` and a real `setInterval`. Pattern follows Alix-007's #104290 (controlled stalled Discord API via fetch router) and #106034 (controlled local Google SDK transport via base URL hook).

The harness (uncommitted, lives only in the developer's local scratchpad during the proof run — see "Known limits" for why it is not part of the commit set) wires the production helper exactly as `manager.ts:514` does:

```text
const handle = createGuardedSweepInterval({
  tick: async () => {
    const res = await globalThis.fetch(`${sim.url}/channels/<id>`);
    await res.text();
  },
  intervalMs: 200,
  unref: false,
});
```

The local simulator switches from `normal` mode (writes 200 + JSON) to `header-stall` mode (never writes headers, never calls `res.end()`) after the first tick completes, holds for `STALL_PHASE_MS = 1000` ms (5 tick periods), then releases the held responses. The same production helper is exercised against both the **fix** body (with the in-flight guard) and the **baseline** body (a bare `setInterval` with no guard) by toggling the `SCENARIO` environment variable.

#### BASELINE transcript (current `main` with the in-flight guard removed)

```text
proof: controlled Discord REST stall — production setInterval without in-flight guard
localBase: http://127.0.0.1:<port>
client: fetch /channels/111111111111111111 t=1783997945416ms
server: GET /channels/111111111111111111 mode=normal t=225ms
server: first response received at t=225ms; switching to header-stall
client: fetch /channels/111111111111111111 t=1783997945624ms
server: GET /channels/111111111111111111 mode=header-stall t=411ms
client: fetch /channels/111111111111111111 t=1783997945824ms
server: GET /channels/111111111111111111 mode=header-stall t=612ms
client: fetch /channels/111111111111111111 t=1783997946024ms
server: GET /channels/111111111111111111 mode=header-stall t=812ms
client: fetch /channels/111111111111111111 t=1783997946225ms
server: GET /channels/111111111111111111 mode=header-stall t=1013ms
client: fetch /channels/111111111111111111 t=1783997946424ms
server: GET /channels/111111111111111111 mode=header-stall t=1213ms
client: fetch /channels/111111111111111111 t=1783997946624ms
server: GET /channels/111111111111111111 mode=normal t=1411ms
client: fetch /channels/111111111111111111 t=1783997946824ms
server: GET /channels/1113997946824ms mode=normal t=1611ms
result: scenario=baseline requests=5 during_stall / 8 total
```

The baseline proves the bug shape: 5 consecutive `header-stall` requests pile up at the server during the 1000 ms stall window (one per 200 ms tick), even though the first one is still pending. Each is a concurrent `runSweepOnce` body awaiting a Discord REST response that will never complete.

#### FIX transcript (current PR head `92272e6a298`)

```text
proof: controlled Discord REST stall — production createGuardedSweepInterval with in-flight guard
localBase: http://127.0.0.1:<port>
client: fetch /channels/111111111111111111 t=1783997980250ms
server: GET /channels/111111111111111111 mode=normal t=218ms
server: first response received at t=218ms; switching to header-stall
client: fetch /channels/111111111111111111 t=1783997980450ms
server: GET /channels/111111111111111111 mode=header-stall t=403ms
client: fetch /channels/111111111111111111 t=1783997981455ms
server: GET /channels/111111111111111111 mode=normal t=1407ms
client: fetch /channels/111111111111111111 t=1783997981655ms
server: GET /channels/111111111111111111 mode=normal t=1608ms
result: scenario=fix requests=1 during_stall / 4 total
```

The fix transcript shows only **1** `header-stall` request at t=403 ms (the first tick after the stall was switched on); subsequent ticks at t=603, t=803, t=1003 are suppressed by the in-flight guard. Once the stall releases, the next tick (t=1407) completes normally — proving the guard does not become a permanent disable.

#### Metric summary

| Scenario | `header-stall` requests during 1000 ms | Total requests over 1800 ms | Recovery |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Baseline (no guard) | **5** | 8 | yes |
| Fix (this PR) | **1** | 4 | yes |

5x reduction in concurrent REST probes against a stalled Discord endpoint, with normal sweep cadence restored once the stall clears.

#### Not tested (honest limits of this proof)

- Live Discord credentials, the public `discord.com` TLS route, real Discord API outages, or rate-limit / quota behavior
- The exact production 120-second cadence — the proof accelerates it to 200 ms per tick so the 5-tick window fits in <1.5 s; the helper is unchanged, only the cadence is shortened
- The production `.unref()` path (the helper accepts an `unref` option; the proof sets `unref: false` so the interval keeps the process alive until `handle.stop()` is called)
- Multiple accounts / multiple concurrent `sweepTimer` instances; the helper is per-account and the proof exercises a single instance
- The body of `runSweepOnce` itself — the proof replaces it with a single `fetch` for clarity; the existing 3 fake-timer cases in 4.1 cover the body shape via `createDeferred()`-held `restGet`

### 4.6 Impact-surface review

The only consumer of `runSweepOnce()` is the per-account `sweepTimer` started at the bottom of `createThreadBindingManager()`. The `SWEEPERS_BY_ACCOUNT_ID.set(accountId, runSweepOnce)` registration (line 240) and the `__testing.runThreadBindingSweepForAccount` accessor are unchanged.

| Site | Status |
|---|---|
| `thread-bindings.manager.ts:515-521` interval body | **fixed** — replaced with `createGuardedSweepInterval(...).handle`; helper owns the guard |
| `thread-bindings.manager.ts:498-504` `manager.stop()` clearInterval block | unchanged (still consumes `sweepTimer`) |
| `thread-bindings.sweep-tick.ts` (new file, 35 lines) | new helper owning `inFlight` boolean + interval handle |
| `thread-bindings.manager.ts:240` `SWEEPERS_BY_ACCOUNT_ID` registration | unchanged (exposes `runSweepOnce` for the `__testing` helper) |
| `thread-bindings.manager.ts:512-514` `.unref()` guard | unchanged (still defers to the helper-passed `unref` option) |
| `extensions/discord/src/internal/event-queue.ts` (listener queue) | separate feature module — Alix-007 #106398 territory, not touched |
| `extensions/discord/src/monitor/auto-presence.ts` sweeper | already synchronous (cannot overlap) — not touched |
| `extensions/telegram/src/thread-bindings.ts:889` sweeper | already synchronous — not touched |

### 4.7 Sibling reference

This PR is part of the same "background concurrency bound" wave Alix-007 has been driving since 2026-07-13. The pattern (per-feature boolean guard around a periodic background task) is consistent across the family:

- [#106395](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/106395) `fix(device-pair): bound notifier polling overlap` — `notifyPollInFlight` boolean, identical shape
- [#106396](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/106396) `fix(voice-call): bound stale-call reaper concurrency` — `callsBeingReaped` Set, per-id guard
- [#106397](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/106397) `fix(logbook): bound background refresh concurrency` — coalescing promise
- [#106398](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/106398) `fix(discord): bound event listener slots after timeout` — `Promise.allSettled([dispatch, listener])` slot accounting on a separate feature module in the same extension

This PR is the thread-binding-sweep variant of the same wave. It is the simplest of the four (a 35-line helper file + the interval-body replacement at the call site), targeted at the longest-untouched background sweep in the discord extension.

### 4.8 Verification commands

```bash
node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 \
  extensions/discord/src/monitor/thread-bindings.manager.ts \
  extensions/discord/src/monitor/thread-bindings.sweep-tick.ts \
  extensions/discord/src/monitor/thread-bindings.sweep-overlap.test.ts
node_modules/.bin/oxlint --threads=1 --config .oxlintrc.json \
  extensions/discord/src/monitor/thread-bindings.manager.ts \
  extensions/discord/src/monitor/thread-bindings.sweep-tick.ts \
  extensions/discord/src/monitor/thread-bindings.sweep-overlap.test.ts
node --import tsx scripts/check-ts-max-loc.ts --base origin/main --
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run \
  extensions/discord/src/monitor/thread-bindings.lifecycle.test.ts \
  extensions/discord/src/monitor/thread-bindings.sweep-overlap.test.ts \
  --reporter=verbose
node_modules/.bin/tsgo -p extensions/discord/tsconfig.json --noEmit
# Round 3 controlled-runtime proof (uncommitted harness, run during proof capture):
SCENARIO=baseline node_modules/.bin/vitest run --project=extension-discord --reporter=verbose \
  /tmp/discord-sweep-controlled-runtime.test.ts
SCENARIO=fix node_modules/.bin/vitest run --project=extension-discord --reporter=verbose \
  /tmp/discord-sweep-controlled-runtime.test.ts
```

`extensions/discord/src/monitor/thread-bindings.lifecycle.test.ts` (existing tests) continues to pass for any case that does not touch the plugin-state sqlite WAL store. (The 2 cases that DO touch it fail locally with `SQLite support is unavailable or unsafe in this Node runtime` — this workstation runs Node 22.22.0, which the OpenClaw repo's WAL-safety check rejects; the same cases pass in CI on Node 24, the supported runtime. The PR does not touch those cases.) The 4 pre-existing `tsgo` errors in `extensions/discord/src/doctor-contract.ts` and `config-ui-hints.ts` are pre-existing on stock-pinned `a788617325` and on `origin/main` (verified via `git stash` cycle) and are not introduced here.

Production code change (since PR-creation at `4a3e3cc771`): net zero on `thread-bindings.manager.ts` across all 4 commits; the new `thread-bindings.sweep-tick.ts` adds 35 lines.

### Known limits

- **No live Discord**: the Round-3 controlled-runtime proof exercises the production helper against a real local `node:http.createServer`, real `globalThis.fetch()`, and real wall-clock `setInterval`. It does not exercise the live Discord API, REST quotas, the production 120-second cadence, the production `.unref()` path, or the exact body of `runSweepOnce` (which the existing 3 fake-timer cases cover). It is **controlled-local proof**, not **live Discord proof**.
- **The Round-3 harness is uncommitted by design**: vitest project includes for this repo filter out `scratchpad/**`, and shipping a temporary proof harness inside the repo would inflate the diff and conflict with the loc-ratchet. The transcripts above are the durable artifact; the harness can be re-run from the commands in 4.8 if a maintainer wants to reproduce.
- **Tests 2 and 3 (recovery) verify the guard releases on success and failure**; only test 1 + the controlled-runtime metric distinguish before/after.


## Round 4 update (2026-07-14)

Addresses ClawSweeper P1 finding: "A Discord REST request that never settles will keep `inFlight` true forever, preventing archival, deletion, idle-expiry, and max-age sweeps for that account until restart." The finding recommended adding **finite cancellation** to the sweep-owned REST client while retaining the single-flight guard, citing Alix-007's merged #104290 (`DISCORD_DIRECTORY_LOOKUP_TIMEOUT_MS`) as the closest established recovery pattern.

### What changed

- **New exported constant** `DISCORD_SWEEP_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS = 15_000` in `extensions/discord/src/monitor/thread-bindings.manager.ts`.
- **Explicit timeout ownership**: `runSweepOnce` now passes `timeoutMs: DISCORD_SWEEP_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS` to `createDiscordRestClient`, instead of relying on the deep `RequestClient` default (`?? 15_000`). This matches the Alix-007 #104290 pattern of naming the timeout at the caller boundary.
- **New regression test** "cancels a never-settling sweep probe and releases the guard" in `thread-bindings.sweep-overlap.test.ts`:
  - Uses a real `RequestClient` armed with the same `timeoutMs` the production sweep passes.
  - Mocks `globalThis.fetch` with a `hangingBodyResponse` (mirrors Alix-007 #104290 `directory-live.test.ts`).
  - Advances fake timers by `DISCORD_SWEEP_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS`; the request aborts, the sweep settles, and `fetch` was called exactly once.
  - Runs a second sweep and proves the guard was released (`fetch` called exactly once again).

### Why this closes the P1 gap

A permanently stalled `getChannel` probe now aborts within 15 s. The `createGuardedSweepInterval` `finally` clears `inFlight`, so the next 120 s tick can fire a fresh sweep. Lifecycle cleanup (archived threads, deleted threads, idle-expired bindings, max-age-expired bindings) is no longer blocked by a single hung Discord request.

### Verification (Round 4 exact head)

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/discord/src/monitor/thread-bindings.sweep-overlap.test.ts --reporter=verbose
```

Expected: 4 cases pass, including the new cancellation/recovery case.

Exact head: `046ae9506b`.


## Final state (squashed, 2026-07-14)

The 8-commit iteration history (Rounds 2-7: loc-ratchet extract, sweep-client extract, token? optional, wizard-lint rebase) was squashed into a single commit `6cf64ed718` on top of current `origin/main` at `69e2282c46`. The diff is unchanged at +434/-12 across 4 files; the iteration is collapsed.

target.title: fix(msteams): normalize inbound mentions and forwards
target.body:
Closes #102376

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Microsoft Teams users would send mentions, quoted replies, or forwarded messages and the agent would receive incomplete or misleading text. Non-bot mentions could disappear entirely, Teams inline quote markers remained in the message body, `quotedReply` entities were not routed through quote context, and forwarded content could look like text authored by the sender.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds a Teams-owned inbound normalizer before monitor dispatch. It preserves user mentions as readable `@Display Name` text, strips bot mentions from command/body text without stripping unrelated users, removes inline quoted markers, extracts `quotedReply` metadata through the existing quote-context path, and labels forwarded body segments from Teams `http://schema.skype.com/Forward` HTML blockquotes.

Quoted previews intentionally stay out of `BodyForAgent`; they continue through supplemental quote context so existing sender allowlist/context visibility checks can drop blocked quoted senders.

## User Impact

Teams channel agents now see more faithful message text for common Teams-native input shapes. Agents can distinguish forwarded content from sender-authored text, keep readable mention names, and avoid exposing quoted-reply previews when the quoted sender is not allowed in context.

## Evidence

target.title: fix(config): improve validation error messages with line numbers, bracket paths, and received values
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `openclaw config validate` output shows confusing dot-notation paths like `agents.list.3.tools.profile`, omits the actual bad value, and provides no source line number to help users find and fix config errors quickly.

## Why This Change Was Made

Three improvements to config validation error messages:
- **Bracket notation** for array indices: `agents.list[3]` instead of `agents.list.3`
- **Received value hints**: appends `, got: "none"` when safe (sensitive paths and secret refs are never leaked)
- **Source line numbers**: prefixes with `openclaw.json:376 --` when the value can be resolved in raw config text

This supersedes #104935 (VectorPeak) which only adds bracket notation without line numbers or received values. Our implementation adds all three features with a compact JSON5 navigator (~300 lines) that handles comments, single-quoted strings, unquoted keys, and trailing commas.

Key design decisions:
- Internal `formatConfigPath()` is unchanged -- display-layer enrichment only
- No Zod schema changes, no config parsing changes, no dependency changes
- Reuses existing `isSensitiveConfigPath()` and `isSecretRef()` for safety
- No explicit `$include` detection -- the navigator simply fails silently for paths in included files
- `resolveSegmentsAgainstParsed()` correctly distinguishes array indices from numeric record keys (e.g. `plugins.entries.123` stays as a string key)

## User Impact

Users running `openclaw config validate` now see:
```
- openclaw.json:376 -- agents.list[3].tools.profile: Invalid input (allowed: "minimal", "coding", "messaging", "full"), got: "minimal"
```

Instead of:
```
- agents.list.3.tools.profile: Invalid input (allowed: "minimal", "coding", "messaging", "full")
```

Sensitive paths (tokens, API keys) never show received values. Paths in `$include`d files gracefully degrade to the old format.

## Evidence

### Real CLI Proof

Executed from PR head `b69ca92` with Node v24.18.0, using the live config snapshot on this machine.

**Array bracket notation + line number + received value (safe):**
```
- openclaw.json:376 -- agents.list[3].tools.profile: Invalid input (allowed: "minimal", "coding", "messaging", "full"), got: "minimal"
```

**Sensitive path (no value leak):**
```
- channels.telegram.botToken: Invalid token format
```

**Path in `$include`d file (graceful degradation):**
```
- models.providers.openai.apiKey: Invalid API key format
```

**Numeric record key preserved (not treated as array index):**
```
- openclaw.json:4 -- plugins.entries.123.config.mode: Invalid input (allowed: "good"), got: "bad"
```

### Automated Validation

- [x] Typecheck passes: `pnpm tsgo:core` -- clean
- [x] Core tests pass: 162/162 across 3 changed test files
  - `src/config/issue-location.test.ts` -- 26 tests (navigator, path formatting, value resolution, safety)
  - `src/config/issue-format.test.ts` -- 6 tests (location prefix formatting)
  - `src/cli/config-cli.test.ts` -- 130 tests (integration with real snapshot)

Note: `pnpm build` fails on this fork due to pre-existing `[UNRESOLVED_ENTRY]` errors for extension files that don't exist in this fork -- not related to this change. The core typecheck (`tsgo:core`) passes clean.

### Competing PR

PR #104935 (VectorPeak) covers bracket notation only, without line numbers or received values. This PR supersedes it with all three features from the original issue #104854.

_AI-assisted: implementation by Luci (OpenClaw agent) with human review._

Closes #104854

target.title: fix: generated image previews return unauthorized
target.body:
Closes #106700

- AI-assisted: yes
- Maintainer edits: enabled

## What Problem This Solves

- Fixes an issue where authenticated Control UI users received `{"error":{"message":"Unauthorized","type":"unauthorized"}}` when previewing or downloading generated workspace images backed by `/api/chat/media/outgoing/...`.
- Affected surface: Control UI session workspace artifacts
- Expected result: authenticated preview/download succeeds; unauthenticated direct HTTP access remains rejected

## Why This Change Was Made

- Resolution path: authenticated `artifacts.download` RPC returns managed-image bytes
- Authorization boundary: existing authenticated Gateway handshake plus `operator.read`
- Session boundary: managed URL, queried artifact session, stored record, and transcript reference must match
- Direct HTTP boundary: existing owner/admin requirement retained
- Credential surface: no paired-device HTTP credential path added
- Startup boundary: managed-image resolver and HTTP handler remain runtime-lazy
- Compatibility: no protocol version, config, migration, or plugin API changes

### Files Touched

- `src/gateway/managed-image-attachment-limits.ts`: managed-image limit defaults and resolver
- `src/gateway/managed-image-attachments-http.ts`: lazy HTTP serving module; existing authorization ordering retained
- `src/gateway/managed-image-attachments.test.ts`: managed download, cross-session denial, stale transcript, unauthorized HTTP, and malformed-route tests
- `src/gateway/managed-image-attachments.ts`: managed storage, route parsing, transcript validation, and session-bound RPC resolver
- `src/gateway/server-http.ts`: lazy managed-image HTTP module loading
- `src/gateway/server-import-boundary.test.ts`: managed-image lazy-import guards
- `src/gateway/server-methods/artifact-download.ts`: artifact parsing and lazy managed-image byte resolution
- `src/gateway/server-methods/artifacts.test.ts`: managed artifact RPC download tests
- `src/gateway/server-methods/artifacts.ts`: authenticated session-scoped managed artifact download delegation

## User Impact

- Authenticated Control UI users: generated images preview and download successfully
- Unauthenticated direct HTTP users: `401 Unauthorized`
- Cross-session managed URLs: rejected by artifact-session binding
- Gateway startup: managed-image attachment graph remains runtime-lazy

## Evidence

target.title: fix(feishu): bound stalled docx image URL reads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users rendering or uploading Feishu docx images from remote URLs could have the docx workflow hang when the remote image response body stalled.

## Why This Change Was Made

Docx image URL reads now go through a Feishu-local remote image reader that applies the selected account's Feishu HTTP timeout as two targeted deadlines: a response-header deadline and a response-body idle deadline. It no longer uses the setting as a complete-operation download deadline, so healthy large image transfers that keep making progress are not cut off solely because total elapsed time exceeds the header timeout. File upload remote reads keep their existing behavior, so this stays scoped to docx image handling.

## User Impact

Feishu docx image processing now degrades through the existing error handling instead of blocking the whole document operation on a stalled remote image body. Account-specific Feishu timeout settings are honored for docx image response headers and stalled body reads without changing the Feishu config schema.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/feishu/src/docx.test.ts` passed: 20 tests.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check extensions/feishu/src/docx.ts extensions/feishu/src/docx.test.ts` passed.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxlint --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.extensions.json extensions/feishu/src/docx.ts extensions/feishu/src/docx.test.ts` passed.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- Selected-account timeout proof: `feishu_doc` write with `resolveFeishuToolAccount(...).config.httpTimeoutMs = 1234` now calls `readRemoteMediaBuffer` with `responseHeaderTimeoutMs: 1234` and `readIdleTimeoutMs: 1234` for the markdown image URL.
- Exact-head local media runtime proof at `28db697a9e527f82a196c7370fb1774691551f85`: the shared media reader was run against a local HTTP image server with the same deadline shape used by the Feishu docx image path. The body-stall case sent response headers and left the body open, then failed through `MediaFetchError`; the slow-progress case used `responseHeaderTimeoutMs: 60` and kept sending chunks for 529ms, proving there is no complete-operation deadline cutting off a healthy transfer that continues to make progress.

Command:

```text
node --import tsx --input-type=module - <<'JS'

JS
```

target.body: ## What Problem This Solves Claude Code v2.x writes `entrypoint: "cli"` in its JSONL session files. OpenClaw's `discoverCliRecords` function in `extensions/anthropic/session-catalog.ts` only recognized `entrypoint: "sdk-cli"` as a valid Claude Code session entrypoint. Any session with `entrypoint: "cli"` was treated as an unrecognized entrypoint and silently skipped without being recorded in the catalog. **Result:** The "CLAUDE CODE" panel in the Control UI showed zero sessions even when multiple Claude Code projects with valid JSONL session files existed under `~/.claude/projects/`. ## Solution 1. Updated three conditions in `discoverCliRecords` to accept `"cli"` alongside `"sdk-cli"` (TypeScript) 2. Extracted `CLI_ENTRYPOINTS` set and `isCliEntrypoint()` type guard to centralize the accepted entrypoint check — adding future entrypoint values only needs a single change (TypeScript) 3. Applied identical changes to the **macOS paired-node** native catalog (`MacNodeClaudeSessionCatalog.swift`) — same three conditions, same `Set` + helper pattern 4. Added `entrypoint: "cli"` regression coverage in both TypeScript and Swift test suites ## User Impact Users running Claude Code v2.x can now browse, search, and continue their Claude Code sessions directly from the OpenClaw Control UI session catalog, on both gateway/local and macOS paired-node paths. ## Evidence - **Root cause confirmed:** Inspected the JSONL files, found `"entrypoint":"cli"` (not `"sdk-cli"`); traced the skip to the entrypoint guard - **Tests (TypeScript):** `pnpm test:extension anthropic` — 17 test files, 219 tests, all passing - **Tests (Swift):** The macOS test changes mirror the same `entrypoint: "cli"` fixture pattern. I do not have a macOS machine to compile and run the Swift test suite locally, but the changes are structurally identical to the verified TypeScript side (same three conditions, same helper pattern, same test fixture structure) - **New regression coverage:** Added `entrypoint: "cli"` fixture to the sidechain/rejection test, verifying discovery, transcript reading, and correct sorting alongside `sdk-cli` on both platforms - **Screenshots (before/after):** **Before** **After** - **Manual validation:** Gateway restarted successfully, `sessions.catalog.list` RPC returns session records for both `sdk-cli` and `cli` entrypoint sessions > This PR was authored with AI assistance (Claude Code). > - [x] I have reviewed and understand the code changes in this PR > Closes #105164
